# Cadence UI — full context

# Cadence UI

> Animation-first React components for shadcn. Base UI + Tailwind CSS v4 + Motion.
> Install with `npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/<id>`. Every component ships its motion contract and a reduced-motion branch.

## Install

```json
{ "registries": { "@cadence": "https://cadence.dev/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

## Rules for agents

- Prefer an existing Cadence component over writing new animation code.
- Read the item's `docs` and `meta.motion` before changing motion.
- Keep the reduced-motion branch; never remove `data-motion`.
- Use presets from `components/cadence/lib/motion.ts`; do not invent durations.
- Cadence is UI only: never pass a schema, resolver, or validation rule to a component (P11).

## Components

- [Button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.md): Commands such as save, submit, and delete. (form, feedback)
- [Badge](https://cadence.dev/r/badge.md): Statuses, counts, and categories. (feedback)
- [Kbd](https://cadence.dev/r/kbd.md): Keyboard shortcuts in tooltips, menus, and command lists. (utility)
- [Separator](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.md): Dividing sections, menu groups, and toolbars. (layout)
- [Label](https://cadence.dev/r/label.md): Naming inputs, selects, and other form controls. (form)
- [Input](https://cadence.dev/r/input.md): Names, emails, search queries, and other short text. (form)
- [Textarea](https://cadence.dev/r/textarea.md): Comments, descriptions, and other longer text. (form)
- [Card](https://cadence.dev/r/card.md): Grouping related content, such as a summary or a record. (layout)
- [Aspect Ratio](https://cadence.dev/r/aspect-ratio.md): Images, videos, and embeds that must keep their shape. (layout)
- [Avatar](https://cadence.dev/r/avatar.md): People in comments, assignees, and member lists. (data)
- [Skeleton](https://cadence.dev/r/skeleton.md): Placeholders while cards, tables, and lists load. (feedback, data)
- [Alert](https://cadence.dev/r/alert.md): Errors, warnings, and page-level status messages. (feedback)
- [Empty](https://cadence.dev/r/empty.md): Lists, tables, and panels with nothing to show yet. (feedback, layout)
- [Item](https://cadence.dev/r/item.md): Rows in lists of files, members, and invoices. (data, layout)
- [Field](https://cadence.dev/r/field.md): Form controls that need a label, help text, and error. (form)
- [Button Group](https://cadence.dev/r/button-group.md): Toolbars and related actions on the same object. (form, layout)
- [Input Group](https://cadence.dev/r/input-group.md): Currency fields, URLs, and inputs with inline actions. (form)
- [Breadcrumb](https://cadence.dev/r/breadcrumb.md): Hierarchy navigation, from the root to the current page. (navigation)
- [Pagination](https://cadence.dev/r/pagination.md): Long result sets, tables, and search results. (navigation)
- [Spinner](https://cadence.dev/r/spinner.md): Short waits such as saving, sending, or publishing. (feedback)
- [Dialog](https://cadence.dev/r/dialog.md): Focused tasks such as renaming, inviting, or confirming. (overlay)
- [Checkbox](https://cadence.dev/r/checkbox.md): Independent yes/no choices and multi-select lists. (form)
- [Radio Group](https://cadence.dev/r/radio-group.md): Choosing one option from a small, fixed set. (form)
- [Switch](https://cadence.dev/r/switch.md): Settings that take effect immediately, such as alerts or visibility. (form)
- [Slider](https://cadence.dev/r/slider.md): Volume, brightness, zoom, and price ranges. (form)
- [Toggle](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle.md): Bold, italic, preview, and other on/off modes. (form)
- [Toggle Group](https://cadence.dev/r/toggle-group.md): Text alignment, view density, and other mode sets. (form)
- [Input OTP](https://cadence.dev/r/input-otp.md): Login codes, email verification, and device pairing. (form)
- [Progress](https://cadence.dev/r/progress.md): Uploads, imports, and other work with a measurable end. (feedback)
- [Alert Dialog](https://cadence.dev/r/alert-dialog.md): Destructive or irreversible actions that need confirmation. (overlay)
- [Popover](https://cadence.dev/r/popover.md): Filters, share links, and other controls tied to a trigger. (overlay)
- [Tooltip](https://cadence.dev/r/tooltip.md): Hints for icon buttons, shortcuts, and truncated values. (overlay)
- [Hover Card](https://cadence.dev/r/hover-card.md): Previews of links, profiles, and repositories. (overlay)
- [Sheet](https://cadence.dev/r/sheet.md): Filters, details, and settings that keep the page in view. (overlay)
- [Drawer](https://cadence.dev/r/drawer.md): Quick tasks on touch screens, such as share or move. (overlay)
- [Select](https://cadence.dev/r/select.md): Choosing one value from a short list of options. (form)
- [Combobox](https://cadence.dev/r/combobox.md): Picking from a long list you can filter by typing. (form)
- [Dropdown Menu](https://cadence.dev/r/dropdown-menu.md): Row actions, filters, and view settings behind one button. (overlay)
- [Context Menu](https://cadence.dev/r/context-menu.md): Right-click actions on a file, row, or canvas. (overlay)
- [Menubar](https://cadence.dev/r/menubar.md): Application menus along the top of a window. (overlay)
- [Code block](https://cadence.dev/r/code-block.md): Install commands, source snippets, and tool output. (ai)
- [Command](https://cadence.dev/r/command.md): Search and run actions from a keyboard-driven command palette. (navigation)
- [Toast](https://cadence.dev/r/toast.md): Transient notifications with accessible actions and dismissal. (feedback)
- [Accordion](https://cadence.dev/r/accordion.md): Reveal related sections while keeping their headings easy to scan. (layout)
- [Collapsible](https://cadence.dev/r/collapsible.md): Reveal optional detail with a standalone disclosure. (layout)
- [Tabs](https://cadence.dev/r/tabs.md): Switch between peer views with a shared selection indicator. (navigation)
- [Table](https://cadence.dev/r/table.md): Invoices, transaction histories, and small collections of structured records. (collection)
- [Carousel](https://cadence.dev/r/carousel.md): A swipeable collection with previous and next controls. (layout)
- [Scroll Area](https://cadence.dev/r/scroll-area.md): Constrained lists and wide content with native scrolling and custom scrollbars. (scroll)
- [Chart](https://cadence.dev/r/chart.md): Responsive data charts with themed tooltips and legends. (collection)
- [Calendar](https://cadence.dev/r/calendar.md): Select dates, multiple days, and ranges with accessible month navigation. (collection)
- [Navigation Menu](https://cadence.dev/r/navigation-menu.md): Site navigation with shared popup content and interruptible sizing. (navigation)
- [Resizable](https://cadence.dev/r/resizable.md): Adjustable split panels with pointer and keyboard resizing. (layout)
- [Sidebar](https://cadence.dev/r/sidebar.md): Workspace navigation for dashboards and application shells. (navigation)
- [Data Table](https://cadence.dev/r/data-table.md): An editable payments table with sorting, filtering, selection, visibility, and pagination. (collection)
- [Date Picker](https://cadence.dev/r/date-picker.md): Choose a single date or date range from an anchored calendar. (collection)
- [Attachment](https://cadence.dev/r/attachment.md): Displays file media, metadata, caller-owned upload state, and actions. (ai)
- [Bubble](https://cadence.dev/r/bubble.md): Displays conversational content with variants, grouping, reactions, and polymorphic surfaces. (ai)
- [Table of Contents](https://cadence.dev/r/toc.md): Section navigation for documentation, guides, and long articles. (navigation)

# Button

Commands such as save, submit, and delete.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Save() {
  return <Button>Save changes</Button>;
}
```

## Variants

`variant` sets the visual weight. There are six, and the default one is the primary action of
the surface it sits on; reach for a different weight only when the hierarchy asks for it.

| Variant | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | The one primary action on the surface. |
| `secondary` | A supporting action next to the primary one. |
| `outline` | A neutral action that should not compete for attention. |
| `ghost` | Toolbar and icon-row actions, where the surface carries the shape. |
| `destructive` | An action that removes or overwrites data. |
| `link` | An in-flow action that reads as text. |

<ComponentExample name="variants" />

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Variants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
      <Button>Default</Button>
      <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
      <Button variant="destructive">Destructive</Button>
      <Button variant="outline">Outline</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost">Ghost</Button>
      <Button variant="link">Link</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

`size` sets the height and padding. Four text sizes cover dense toolbars through page-level
calls to action; four square sizes cover icon-only buttons.

| Size | Height | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` | 24px | Dense toolbars and table rows. |
| `sm` | 32px | Secondary actions in compact layouts. |
| `default` | 36px | Most buttons. |
| `lg` | 40px | Page-level calls to action. |
| `icon-xs` | 24px | Icon only, dense. |
| `icon-sm` | 32px | Icon only, compact. |
| `icon` | 36px | Icon only, default. |
| `icon-lg` | 40px | Icon only, prominent. |

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import { MoreHorizontalIcon, PlusIcon, SearchIcon, SettingsIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Sizes() {
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-6">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        <Button size="xs">Extra small</Button>
        <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
        <Button>Default</Button>
        <Button size="lg">Large</Button>
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        <Button size="icon-xs" variant="ghost" aria-label="More"><MoreHorizontalIcon /></Button>
        <Button size="icon-sm" variant="outline" aria-label="Search"><SearchIcon /></Button>
        <Button size="icon" variant="outline" aria-label="Add item"><PlusIcon /></Button>
        <Button size="icon-lg" aria-label="Open settings"><SettingsIcon /></Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Icon-only buttons always need an `aria-label`: the glyph is not a name.

## Links

For navigation, keep the link and take the styles: this preserves link semantics and
middle-click.

<ComponentExample name="links" />

```tsx
import { buttonVariants } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Links() {
  return <a href="/components" className={buttonVariants({ variant: "outline" })}>Browse components</a>;
}
```

## Composition

`render` replaces the underlying element; use it for custom button components, not for links.

The default button forwards native React events, including CSS `onAnimationStart`
and HTML `onDrag` / `onDragStart` / `onDragEnd`. These handlers receive native
React events; press feedback does not call them as animation lifecycle hooks.

<ComponentExample name="composition" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { type ComponentProps, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

function CustomButton(props: ComponentProps<"button">) {
  return <button type="button" {...props} />;
}

export function Composition() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Button render={<CustomButton />} onClick={() => setCount((value) => value + 1)}>
      Count: {count}
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

Use `disabled` while an action is unavailable. Keep the reason or current task in the label;
the component does not manage loading or application state for you.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Disabled() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
      <Button disabled>Saving changes</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" disabled>Unavailable</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- The primary action of a form, dialog, or toolbar.
- A single, clearly labelled command: save, delete, invite.
- Anywhere the user expects a physical press response.

## When not to use

- Navigation between routes; use a link styled with `buttonVariants`.
- Toggling a persistent state; use `toggle` or `switch`.
- Submitting a long-running job that needs its own progress surface; pair the button with a
  spinner and a `disabled` state, or use `toast` for the result.

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "destructive" \| "outline" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "link"` | `"default"` | Visual weight. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "xs" \| "sm" \| "lg" \| "icon" \| "icon-xs" \| "icon-sm" \| "icon-lg"` | `"default"` | Height and padding. |
| `render` | `ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement` | – | Base UI composition; replaces `asChild`. |
| `className` | string or state callback | – | Merged last. |

All native button props are forwarded.

Base UI state callbacks for `className` are evaluated before merging caller classes last.
`style` accepts an object or a state callback and is forwarded to the primitive.

The default press button preserves native React `onAnimationStart`, `onDrag`,
`onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` events, including capture and cancellation. Callback
and object refs follow the same button; replacing a callback runs its React 19
cleanup before assigning the next ref. A caller `render` replaces the default
renderer and owns spreading its supplied props.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`, driven by the press gesture.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| press | `scale 1 → 0.97` while active | `feedback.press` / `spring.press` | yes (pointer up) |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` / `spring.press` | yes |
| reduced | no scale; colour and shadow only | – | – |
| none | no scale; colour and shadow only | – | – |

## Accessibility

- Renders a real `<button>` through Base UI, so Enter and Space activate it natively.
- Focus is visible through the ring tokens; disabled buttons are not focusable and keep
  `aria-disabled` semantics from Base UI.
- `aria-invalid` drives the destructive border and ring. The component does not validate
  anything — rules, schemas, and error copy stay in your form code; [Field](/components/field)
  shows the pairing.

## Responsiveness and performance

Buttons size to their label and selected size; the caller owns wrapping or stacking
an action row on small screens. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. Base UI
activation and Motion press feedback require hydration; native button/link semantics
remain browser-owned in server markup. Press feedback uses transform through
feedback.press, with no layout interpolation. The T1 check budgets this item's own
shipped source at 6 KiB gzip, excluding installed dependencies and application code.

## Notes for AI

- Keep the label specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not add a `loading` boolean that hides the label; pass `disabled` and render a spinner
  next to the text so the action stays readable.

# Badge

Statuses, counts, and categories.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/badge
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";

export function Release() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      <span className="font-medium">Parity plan</span>
      <Badge variant="secondary">0.2.0</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Variants

Choose one of six visual weights for a status or category. The `link` variant is
only a style; use `render` when the badge should navigate.

<ComponentExample name="variants" />

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";

export function BadgeVariants() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Badge>Default</Badge>
      <Badge variant="secondary">Secondary</Badge>
      <Badge variant="destructive">Destructive</Badge>
      <Badge variant="outline">Outline</Badge>
      <Badge variant="ghost">Ghost</Badge>
      <Badge variant="link">Link</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## With an icon

Pair a short label with an icon; the text still communicates the status without
depending on the icon or colour.

<ComponentExample name="icon" />

```tsx
import { CheckIcon, ClockIcon, GitBranchIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";

export function BadgeIcons() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Badge><CheckIcon />Verified</Badge>
      <Badge variant="secondary"><ClockIcon />Pending</Badge>
      <Badge variant="outline"><GitBranchIcon />main</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## As a link

`render` replaces the element, so a badge stays a `span` unless you ask for
something else. The `[a&]` selectors only switch on hover when it really is a link.
These anchors use native focus and Enter navigation to the changelog.

<ComponentExample name="link" />

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";

export function BadgeLinks() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <Badge variant="outline" render={<a href="/docs/changelog" />}>3 releases</Badge>
      <Badge variant="ghost" render={<a href="/docs/changelog" />}>Changelog</Badge>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A short status: `Active`, `Beta`, `Deprecated`, `3 open`.
- A category or tag next to a title, where the colour carries the grouping.
- A count attached to a navigation item or a filter chip.

## When not to use

- Anything the user must click to act; use `button` (a badge has no focus, no
  press feedback, and no keyboard path).
- More than about three words. A long label belongs in running text or in a `card`
  header, not in a pill.
- A status that changes while the user watches; use `toast` or an inline message,
  because a badge swap is easy to miss.

## API

| Prop        | Type                                                                                             | Default     | Description                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "secondary" \| "outline" \| "ghost" \| "destructive" \| "link"`                     | `"default"` | Visual weight.                                   |
| `render`    | `ReactElement \| (props, state) => ReactElement`                                                  | –           | Base UI composition; replaces `asChild`.         |
| `className` | `string`                                                                                          | –           | Merged last.                                     |

`data-slot="badge"` and `data-variant` are rendered from the component's state, so
you can restyle per variant from CSS without touching this file. All native span
props are forwarded.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A badge labels content; it does not enter, leave, or move.

| Phase   | Properties                          | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ----------------------------------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none                                | –     | –             |
| reduced | none                                | –     | –             |
| none    | none                                | –     | –             |

`transition-[color,box-shadow]` is state feedback on the design tokens (hover on a
linked badge, the focus ring), not motion: it never moves the box and never runs
on mount.

## Accessibility

- The badge is a `span`, so it is not in the tab order and has no role — the text
  itself is the message.
- Colour is never the only signal: every variant still carries readable text.
- When rendered as a link it inherits the anchor's semantics, focus ring, and
  keyboard behaviour, and gains `[a&]:hover` styles automatically.

## Responsiveness and performance

Badges keep intrinsic width and do not wrap their text. Keep labels short; let the parent wrap a
collection or provide an overflow strategy for long labels.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Never attach `onClick` to a badge; switch to `button` with `size="sm"`.
- Do not animate a badge in or out. If the status changes, swap the text and let
  `aria-live` on the surrounding region announce it.

# Kbd

Keyboard shortcuts in tooltips, menus, and command lists.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/kbd
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd";

export function ShortcutHint() {
  return (
    <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
      Search <KbdGroup><Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd></KbdGroup>
    </span>
  );
}
```

## Single key

Use one `Kbd` for one physical key. It is a hint, with no focus stop or keyboard handler.

<ComponentExample name="single" />

```tsx
import { Kbd } from "@/components/cadence/kbd";

export function EscapeHint() {
  return <Kbd>Esc</Kbd>;
}
```

## A combination

`KbdGroup` renders the keys with one gap between them and keeps the sequence
together for screen readers.

<ComponentExample name="combination" />

```tsx
import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd";

export function CommandHint() {
  return (
    <KbdGroup>
      <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
      <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>
      <Kbd>P</Kbd>
    </KbdGroup>
  );
}
```

## Inside a tooltip

A `Kbd` inside `data-slot="tooltip-content"` inverts its colours automatically, so
the hint stays legible on the tooltip surface.
Focus or hover the trigger to see it. Install `@cadence/tooltip` and `@cadence/button`
for this composition; the application owns any save action or shortcut handler.
Tooltip and Button keep their own motion contracts and inherit the site's motion settings.

<ComponentExample name="tooltip" />

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd";
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";

export function SaveHint() {
  return (
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Save changes</TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>
        Save <KbdGroup><Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>S</Kbd></KbdGroup>
      </TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A shortcut hinted next to a command: search, save, new item.
- A key the user should press in a flow: `Tab`, `Esc`, `↑ ↓`.
- Inside a `tooltip` or a `dropdown-menu` item, where space is short.

## When not to use

- A key that is part of running text. Write it in prose; a pill interrupts the
  sentence.
- A button that runs a command. A `kbd` is a label, not a control — it has no
  keyboard path and no press state.
- Long sequences of more than three keys. Put the shortcut in a table instead.

## API

| Part       | Props                        | Notes                                            |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Kbd`      | native `kbd` props           | One key. `data-slot="kbd"`.                      |
| `KbdGroup` | native `div` props           | Wraps several keys with `data-slot="kbd-group"`. |

KbdGroup keeps the pinned native div prop type while rendering a `kbd` element.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A key hint is a label; it must not pulse or slide while the user
is reading it.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- Renders a real `<kbd>` element, which assistive technology reports as keyboard
  input — the same information a sighted user reads from the key shape.
- The shortcut is text, so it survives every reduced-motion mode and every colour
  theme.
- If a hint is icon-only, put the key name in `aria-label` on the `Kbd`.
- Do not attach `tabIndex`; a shortcut hint is not focusable.

## Responsiveness and performance

Keys and key groups use intrinsic inline sizes. The caller owns wrapping or scrolling long shortcut
descriptions; these labels do not register keyboard shortcuts.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not
imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for
this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Use the platform's own glyphs (`⌘`, `⇧`, `↵`) rather than words, and keep one
  `Kbd` per physical key.
- If the shortcut is a live command, render a `button` and put the `Kbd` inside it.

# Separator

Dividing sections, menu groups, and toolbars.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/separator
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@/components/cadence/separator";

export function Account() {
  return (
    <div className="space-y-4">
      <p className="text-sm">Signed in as ada@example.com</p>
      <Separator />
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Billing is handled by finance.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Horizontal

The default horizontal separator fills the available width and announces a
boundary between groups. Its parent controls the width and spacing.

<ComponentExample name="horizontal" />

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@/components/cadence/separator";

export function AccountBoundary() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-3 text-sm">
      <span>Signed in as ada@example.com.</span>
      <Separator />
      <span className="text-muted-foreground">Billing is handled by finance.</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Vertical

A vertical rule needs a height from its container. Here its full height comes
from the explicitly sized row; it keeps the vertical orientation in the accessibility tree.

<ComponentExample name="vertical" />

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@/components/cadence/separator";

export function DraftBoundary() {
  return (
    <div className="flex h-6 items-center gap-3 text-sm">
      <span>Draft</span>
      <Separator orientation="vertical" />
      <span className="text-muted-foreground">Edited 2 minutes ago</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Decorative

Upstream's Base UI separator is always announced. Mark a purely visual rule as
decorative so screen readers skip it:

<ComponentExample name="decorative" />

```tsx
import { Separator } from "@/components/cadence/separator";

export function VisualRule() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-72 gap-3 text-sm">
      <span>Cadence UI</span>
      <Separator decorative />
      <span className="text-muted-foreground">Made for your next project.</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Between groups inside a menu, a card footer, or a settings list.
- Between a toolbar and its content, horizontally or vertically.
- Inside a stack of sections that would otherwise merge visually.

## When not to use

- To create space. Use padding or `gap`; a rule is a boundary, not a spacer.
- Between every list item. Repetition turns a boundary into noise — grouped
  spacing does the same job with less ink.
- As a decorative flourish in a hero. That is a background, not a separator.

## API

| Prop          | Type                         | Default          | Description                                                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"`   | Direction of the rule.                                        |
| `decorative`  | `boolean`                    | `false`          | Renders `role="none"` and `aria-hidden`; additive to upstream. |
| `render`      | Base UI render prop          | –                | Composition, as on every Base UI primitive.                   |
| `className`   | string or state callback                     | –                | Merged last.                                                  |

`data-slot="separator"` and `data-orientation` are always set, so a consumer can
size the rule from CSS: `data-[orientation=vertical]:h-8`.

Base UI state callbacks for `className` are evaluated before merging caller classes last.
`style` accepts an object or a state callback and is forwarded to the primitive.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A boundary that animates draws the eye to the wrong thing; if the
layout changes, the surrounding `accordion` or `collapsible` owns that animation.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, which is the
  correct semantic for a group boundary.
- `decorative` removes it from the accessibility tree for rules that carry no
  meaning (a divider inside a visual layout).
- Focusable separators are not supported on purpose: a rule is not a control.

## Responsiveness and performance

Horizontal separators fill available width; vertical separators need a parent with a defined height.
Orientation is caller-owned, with no automatic breakpoint.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Prefer `gap` and `space-y` first; add a separator only when two groups need a
  visible boundary.
- Never place a separator between two items of the same list. Group the list
  instead.

# Label

Naming inputs, selects, and other form controls.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/label
```

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function EmailField() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Email</Label>
      <Input id={id} type="email" autoComplete="email" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Wrapping instead of `htmlFor`

Either association works: `htmlFor` + `id`, or wrapping the control. Pick one per
field and keep it consistent.
This example wraps a native checkbox and needs no `id` or `htmlFor`. Clicking the
words toggles that checkbox; it does not affect the separate checkbox above.

<ComponentExample name="wrapping" />

```tsx
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function WrappedPreference() {
  return (
    <Label>
      <input type="checkbox" defaultChecked />
      Email me about releases
    </Label>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

The label follows the control without any prop: `peer-disabled:` handles a sibling
control placed before the label; `group-data-[disabled=true]:` handles a disabled group.
These two arrangements show both relationships. Set `disabled` on the actual
control; styling a label never disables an input. `useId` keeps repeated fields independent.

<ComponentExample name="disabled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function DisabledFields() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
      <div className="group grid w-56 gap-2" data-disabled="true">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-slug`}>Slug</Label>
        <Input id={`${id}-slug`} disabled defaultValue="cadence" />
      </div>
      <div className="grid w-56 gap-2">
        <Input id={`${id}-workspace`} className="peer" disabled defaultValue="Cadence UI" />
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-workspace`}>Workspace</Label>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Every input, textarea, select, checkbox, radio, switch, and slider that needs a
  visible name.
- A group of controls that share one caption.
- A field whose purpose is not obvious from the placeholder alone (which is
  almost every field).

## When not to use

- As a placeholder. A placeholder disappears on the first keystroke and is not a
  name; use a real `Label`.
- As a heading. If the text introduces a section, use a heading so it appears in
  the document outline.
- For helper text or error text; those belong in the description/error slot so
  they can be wired through `aria-describedby`.

## API

| Prop        | Type              | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `htmlFor`   | `string`          | –       | Id of the control this label names.  |
| `className` | `string`          | –       | Merged last.                         |

All native `label` props are forwarded.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A label is text; the only thing it reacts to is the disabled state,
which is an opacity change on a token, not an animation.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- Renders a native `<label>`; clicking it focuses the control with no JavaScript.
- The accessible name comes from the label's text, so never hide it with
  `display: none`. If the design needs a hidden label, use `sr-only`, not removal.
- `htmlFor` must point at an `id` that exists in the same document. Duplicate ids
  break the association silently.

## Responsiveness and performance

Labels use flex layout and inherit their available width. Keep long labels readable beside controls;
the caller owns stacking and responsive field layout.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not
imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for
this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- One label per control. Do not add `aria-label` on the control as well; two names
  fight, and the visible one wins in some browsers and loses in others.
- Keep the label short and noun-shaped ("Email", "Workspace name"), and put the
  explanation in the description slot.

# Input

Names, emails, search queries, and other short text.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function WorkspaceName() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="workspace">Workspace name</Label>
      <Input id="workspace" placeholder="Acme" autoComplete="organization" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Invalid

The caller supplies `aria-invalid` and a described error. This fixed error state does not run validation or prevent editing.

<ComponentExample name="invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function InvalidInput() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Email</Label>
      <Input id={id} type="email" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby={`${id}-error`} defaultValue="ada@" />
      <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-destructive">Enter a complete email address.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## File input

Use the native file picker for caller-owned files. `accept` suggests file types; the browser and your application own selection, upload and checks.

<ComponentExample name="file" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function FileInput() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Image</Label>
      <Input id={id} type="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg" aria-describedby={`${id}-hint`} />
      <p id={`${id}-hint`} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Choose a PNG or JPEG image.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled, Base UI style

The caller owns `value` through Base UI’s `onValueChange`. The external action replaces only this example’s value; typing in another specimen remains independent.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function ControlledInput() {
  const id = useId();
  const [value, setValue] = useState("");
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-3">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Workspace name</Label>
      <Input id={id} value={value} onValueChange={setValue} aria-describedby={`${id}-value`} />
      <p id={`${id}-value`} role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Value: {value || "(empty)"}</p>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue("Cadence UI")}>Use workspace name</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled and read-only

A disabled field cannot be edited or focused and is omitted from native form submission. A read-only field stays focusable and submits its value. A filled field is still editable unless you explicitly set `readOnly`.

<ComponentExample name="disabled-readonly" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";

export function InputAvailability() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-4">
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-filled`}>Filled</Label>
        <Input id={`${id}-filled`} name="workspace" defaultValue="Cadence UI" />
      </div>
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-disabled`}>Disabled</Label>
        <Input id={`${id}-disabled`} name="disabled" disabled defaultValue="cadence" />
      </div>
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-readonly`}>Read-only</Label>
        <Input id={`${id}-readonly`} name="slug" readOnly defaultValue="cadence-ui" />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A single line of text the user types: email, name, slug, search, URL.
- A field that needs a native input type (`email`, `password`, `tel`, `number`,
  `file`) and therefore native mobile keyboards.
- Anywhere the browser's autofill, password manager, or form submission should
  work without a wrapper.

## When not to use

- Multi-line text; use `textarea`.
- A choice from a fixed list; use `select` (or `combobox` when the list is long).
- A value the app controls entirely, like a generated id. Render text, not a
  disabled input.

## API

| Prop            | Type                                | Default | Description                                        |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`          | `string`                            | –       | Native input type.                                 |
| `value`         | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | –   | Controlled value.                                  |
| `defaultValue`  | same as `value`                     | –       | Uncontrolled initial value.                        |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string, details) => void`  | –       | Base UI change callback, in addition to `onChange`. |
| `className`     | string or state callback                            | –       | Merged last.                                       |

All native input props are forwarded, including `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`,
and `aria-*`.

Base UI state callbacks for `className` are evaluated before merging caller classes last.
`style` accepts an object or a state callback and is forwarded to the primitive.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). An input that grows, slides, or fades while the user types is a
bug: it moves the caret under the user's eyes.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

`transition-[color,box-shadow]` exists for the focus ring and the invalid border.
Both are colour/shadow state feedback on the design tokens, take no space, and do
not run on mount.

## Accessibility

- Base UI's input is field-aware: inside a `field`, it receives the label id and
  the description ids without extra wiring.
- Always give it a name from a `label`; a placeholder is not a name.
- `aria-invalid` plus a described error is the accessible failure state. Colour
  alone is never the signal.
- Never set `outline: none` in `className`; the focus ring is the only affordance
  for keyboard users.

## Validation and data ownership

P11 draws the line: the component renders state, the user decides state.

| The component does                                    | You do                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid="true"` and `data-invalid`        | Deciding what "valid" means (required, format, length)    |
| Renders whatever `aria-describedby` points at          | Writing the error text and the ids it lives on            |
| Forwards `required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `name`    | Form state (react-hook-form, TanStack Form, server state)  |
| Keeps focus visible and keyboard-reachable             | Submit, retry, error mapping, focus management             |

There is no `schema`, `resolver`, `validate`, or `rules` prop, and no validation
library is imported. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message
are wired.

## Responsiveness and performance

The input fills its parent and uses base text sizing below the md breakpoint. Constrain the parent
in grids; native input types retain browser keyboards, editing and form behavior.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Use `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` — never an `error` prop or internal
  state.
- Do not wrap the input in a div just to add a border; the component already owns
  the border, radius, and focus ring.

# Textarea

Comments, descriptions, and other longer text.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/textarea
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/cadence/textarea";

export function Comment() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor="comment">Comment</Label>
      <Textarea id="comment" rows={4} placeholder="Leave a note for the reviewer" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Auto-growing

`field-sizing-content` lets a supporting browser grow the box as you type. This example caps growth at `max-h-48`, then scrolls its contents. There is no JavaScript resize fallback or height animation.

<ComponentExample name="auto-growing" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/cadence/textarea";

export function GrowingTextarea() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Growing note</Label>
      <Textarea id={id} className="min-h-16 max-h-48" placeholder="Type another line…" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Resizable by the user

`field-sizing-fixed` opts out of content-driven sizing so the browser’s vertical resize handle controls the height. `resize-y` preserves the parent’s width; the minimum and maximum keep resizing bounded.

<ComponentExample name="resizable" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/cadence/textarea";

export function ResizableTextarea() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Resizable note</Label>
      <Textarea id={id} rows={3} className="field-sizing-fixed resize-y min-h-24 max-h-64" defaultValue="Drag the lower corner to make more room." />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Invalid

The caller supplies the invalid attribute and error text. Editing keeps the supplied error state until the caller changes it; Textarea does not evaluate the message.

<ComponentExample name="invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/cadence/textarea";

export function InvalidTextarea() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Biography</Label>
      <Textarea id={id} aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby={`${id}-error`} defaultValue="I build design systems that…" />
      <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-destructive">Keep it under 280 characters.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled and read-only

Disabled fields cannot be edited or focused and are omitted from native form submission. Read-only text stays focusable and selectable and remains part of submission.

<ComponentExample name="disabled-readonly" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/cadence/textarea";

export function TextareaAvailability() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-4">
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-disabled`}>Disabled</Label>
        <Textarea id={`${id}-disabled`} name="disabled" disabled defaultValue="Editing is unavailable." />
      </div>
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${id}-readonly`}>Read-only</Label>
        <Textarea id={`${id}-readonly`} name="summary" readOnly defaultValue="The release notes are ready for review." />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled value and character count

The caller owns the text, native `maxLength` and its described character count. The external action replaces only this draft. This counter communicates the limit without adding a validation API.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label";
import { Textarea } from "@/components/cadence/textarea";

export function ControlledTextarea() {
  const id = useId();
  const [value, setValue] = useState("");
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-3">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>Review note</Label>
      <Textarea id={id} value={value} onChange={(event) => setValue(event.target.value)} maxLength={280} aria-describedby={`${id}-count`} />
      <p id={`${id}-count`} role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{value.length} / 280 characters</p>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue("Ready for review.")}>Use review note</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A sentence or a paragraph: a comment, a description, a commit message, a note.
- A field where the user's text is longer than the visible box should be.
- Anywhere the browser's native resize handle is useful.

## When not to use

- A single line (email, name, slug); use `input`.
- Rich text. A `textarea` holds plain text; formatting needs an editor, which is
  out of scope for this library.
- A value that must stay fixed in height; a `textarea` grows, and a fixed box hides
  the overflow from the user.

## API

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description               |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last.              |

All native `textarea` props are forwarded, including `rows`, `maxLength`,
`required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, and `aria-*`.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). Growth is the browser sizing the box, not an animation: on a
`field-sizing-content` textarea the height changes with the text as you type, and
a transition on it would lag behind the caret.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- Renders a native `<textarea>`, so Enter inserts a newline and Escape does not
  close anything — expected behaviour in a form.
- Give it a `label`, and never rely on the placeholder as a name.
- If you cap the length with `maxLength`, say so in the description; a silent stop
  in typing reads as a broken field.
- `resize-y` keeps the horizontal layout stable; full `resize` lets a long word
  break the page.

## Validation and data ownership

Same contract as `input`: the field renders state, you own the state.

| The component does                                 | You do                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid="true"`                       | Deciding validity (length, format, required)             |
| Renders what `aria-describedby` points at           | Writing the error text and the counter ("12 / 280")      |
| Forwards `required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `name` | Form state and submission                                |

Character counters are yours to render: the component does not count. Keep the
count in the description slot and point `aria-describedby` at it, so a screen
reader hears it before the limit is hit.

## Responsiveness and performance

The textarea fills its parent, has a minimum height and uses CSS field-sizing-content where
supported. The browser owns growth and user resizing; provide a height or overflow policy for long
text when needed. There is no JavaScript auto-grow fallback.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not
imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for
this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Do not implement auto-resize with a `scrollHeight` loop; `field-sizing-content`
  is the CSS-only answer and it matches upstream.
- Never own the character count in component state. Render it next to the field and
  wire it through `aria-describedby`.

# Card

Grouping related content, such as a summary or a record.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/card
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardFooter,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from "@/components/cadence/card";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Plan() {
  return (
    <Card className="max-w-sm">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Parity plan</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>58 components, ten batches, one release train.</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Batch B1 ships the eleven atoms.</p>
      </CardContent>
      <CardFooter>
        <Button variant="outline">Open plan</Button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Action in the header

`CardHeader` uses two columns when `CardAction` is present. Keep the action a real link or button; the card surface itself is not a keyboard control.

<ComponentExample name="header-action" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@/components/cadence/card";

export function CardHeaderAction() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-full max-w-sm">
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Workspace setup</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Connect your first project.</CardDescription>
        <CardAction><Button size="sm" variant="outline" render={<a href="/docs/installation" />}>Setup</Button></CardAction>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>Install a component to get started.</CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Compact

`size="sm"` tightens the shared spacing for every part. Compare default and small cards directly; size changes density, not content or a responsive breakpoint.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@/components/cadence/card";

export function CardSizes() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
      {(["default", "sm"] as const).map((size) => (
        <Card key={size} size={size}>
          <CardHeader><CardTitle>{size === "sm" ? "Compact" : "Default"}</CardTitle><CardDescription>Workspace summary</CardDescription></CardHeader>
          <CardContent>Every part follows one spacing property.</CardContent>
          <CardFooter><span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">size=&quot;{size}&quot;</span></CardFooter>
        </Card>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Content-sized

`fit="content"` measures its own flow box with a ResizeObserver and applies the height immediately, even in a stretching grid. Toggle the caller-owned text to compare it with a normal card; the same shell and caller ref remain in place. Narrowing the parent wraps the text and remeasures it. This is geometry, with no animation in any mode. Use it when differing content heights carry information; ordinary card grids usually should line up.

<ComponentExample name="content-sized" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@/components/cadence/card";

export function ContentSizedCard() {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);
  const fitRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg grid-cols-1 items-stretch gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
      <Card fit="content" ref={fitRef} data-testid="fit-card" className="max-w-sm">
        <CardHeader><CardTitle>Content fit</CardTitle></CardHeader>
        <CardContent>{expanded ? "The surface follows its own content immediately. A caller ref still reaches the same measured shell while the text wraps as the viewport narrows." : "Short content."}</CardContent>
        <CardFooter><Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setExpanded((value) => !value)}>Toggle content</Button></CardFooter>
      </Card>
      <Card>
        <CardHeader><CardTitle>Normal grid item</CardTitle><CardDescription>This card stretches with its row.</CardDescription></CardHeader>
        <CardContent>A longer summary can fill more vertical space. The content-sized neighbour keeps its own measured height rather than inheriting this card’s height.</CardContent>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Section boundaries

Add `border-b` to the header and `border-t` to the footer. The parts already adjust their padding for those boundaries, without introducing another Card part.

<ComponentExample name="boundaries" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";
import { Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@/components/cadence/card";

export function CardBoundaries() {
  return (
    <Card className="w-full max-w-sm">
      <CardHeader className="border-b"><CardTitle>Release notes</CardTitle><CardDescription>Review the latest changes.</CardDescription></CardHeader>
      <CardContent>Components, fixes and documentation updates.</CardContent>
      <CardFooter className="border-t"><Button variant="outline" render={<a href="/docs/changelog" />}>Read changelog</Button></CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A unit of content that belongs together: a summary, a plan, an account, a
  record in a grid.
- A surface that needs a header, an optional action, body content, and a footer.
- A list of comparable items where the boundary itself carries meaning.

## When not to use

- To fake spacing. A card is a boundary; use padding if you only need breathing
  room.
- As a page layout. Nesting cards inside cards flattens the hierarchy.
- For a modal or a popover; those are overlays with their own focus rules.

## API

| Part              | Props                           | Notes                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Card`            | `size`, `fit`, native div props | `size` sets `--card-spacing` and `data-size`; `fit`: `"content"` hugs the content. |
| `CardHeader`      | native div props                | Grid header; reacts to `CardAction` and a bottom border.                           |
| `CardTitle`       | native div props                | Bold, leading-none. Does not create a heading.                                     |
| `CardDescription` | native div props                | Muted supporting text.                                                             |
| `CardAction`      | native div props                | Top-right slot inside the header.                                                  |
| `CardContent`     | native div props                | Body; carries the horizontal padding.                                              |
| `CardFooter`      | native div props                | Bottom row; reacts to a top border.                                                |

Every part sets `data-slot`, so CSS can reach it:
`[&>[data-slot=card-header]]:gap-4`. Under `fit="content"` the parts are wrapped
in one `data-slot="card-flow"` box, which is the element the height is measured
from — style the parts from the shell as before, and the flow box only if you
need the measured layer itself.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A card does not fade, lift, or scale in. If a group of cards should
appear in sequence, that is a page-level `list.stagger` decision made by the parent,
not a property of the card.

`fit="content"` adds no row to the table below: the measured height is applied as
soon as it is known, so there is no phase, no interpolation, and no reduced-motion
branch to keep — the geometry is information, and both modes render it identically.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- `Card` is a plain `div`: no role, no landmark. That is correct for a visual
  grouping — but it means the card is not a navigable region. If a set of cards is
  the main content, wrap it in a `<section>` or a list (`<ul>/<li>`).
- `CardTitle` renders a `div`. When the title belongs in the document outline, put
  a heading inside it: `<CardTitle><h3 …>Parity plan</h3></CardTitle>`, or render
  the card with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title's id.
- A card that is clickable must contain a real link or button; do not put
  `onClick` on the card and call it done — it is invisible to keyboard users.

## Responsiveness and performance

Cards follow their parent layout by default. The caller owns grid columns and narrow-screen
wrapping; size="sm" changes spacing, not a breakpoint. With fit="content", CSS resolves width and a
ResizeObserver measures content height after mount, applying it immediately without interpolation.
SSR uses natural content layout before measurement.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. The optional Card observer is
client code and is disconnected on cleanup. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every
interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own
shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Use `CardFooter` for actions, not a bare `div` — it keeps spacing consistent when
  `size` changes.
- Do not add hover lift to a card that is not interactive. Motion on a static card
  is decoration (P9).
- `fit="content"` is opt-in and per card. A grid of cards is meant to line up; only
  reach for the content-sized variant when the differences between cards are the
  information.

# Aspect Ratio

Images, videos, and embeds that must keep their shape.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/aspect-ratio
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio";

export function Cover() {
  return (
    <AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9} className="overflow-hidden rounded-lg">
      <img src="/cover.jpg" alt="Dashboard preview" className="size-full object-cover" />
    </AspectRatio>
  );
}
```

## Square

Use a ratio of `1` for a square crop. The image fills the reserved frame with `object-cover`; the ratio box owns layout, while the child owns its crop and accessible name. This self-contained illustration can be replaced by your own image.

<ComponentExample name="square" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio";

export function SquareImage() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-48">
      <AspectRatio ratio={1} className="overflow-hidden rounded-full">
        <img src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22 viewBox=%220 0 320 240%22%3E%3Crect width=%22320%22 height=%22240%22 fill=%22%23334155%22/%3E%3Ccircle cx=%22240%22 cy=%2264%22 r=%2228%22 fill=%22%23fbbf24%22/%3E%3Cpath d=%22M0 240V180L100 80L240 240ZM120 240L240 120L320 200V240Z%22 fill=%22%2394a3b8%22/%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Illustrated mountains under a golden sun" className="size-full object-cover" />
      </AspectRatio>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Video

A `16 / 9` frame reserves room for video before it loads. Native controls belong to the media itself and stay usable; there is no autoplay. This silent sample loads from MDN only when requested. Replace its source with your own clip and supply captions when it contains speech.

<ComponentExample name="video" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio";

export function VideoFrame() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md">
      <AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9} className="overflow-hidden rounded-lg bg-muted">
        <video controls preload="none" aria-label="Silent flower video" poster="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22 viewBox=%220 0 320 240%22%3E%3Crect width=%22320%22 height=%22240%22 fill=%22%23334155%22/%3E%3Ccircle cx=%22240%22 cy=%2264%22 r=%2228%22 fill=%22%23fbbf24%22/%3E%3Cpath d=%22M0 240V180L100 80L240 240ZM120 240L240 120L320 200V240Z%22 fill=%22%2394a3b8%22/%3E%3C/svg%3E" className="size-full object-cover">
          <source src="https://interactive-examples.mdn.mozilla.net/media/cc0-videos/flower.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
          <track kind="captions" label="No spoken audio" srcLang="en" src="data:text/vtt,WEBVTT%0A%0A" default />
          Your browser does not support video playback.
        </video>
      </AspectRatio>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Multiple ratios in one grid

`ratio` accepts a positive numeric width divided by height, rather than a finite list of variants. Here `4 / 3`, `1`, and `3 / 4` reserve different shapes at the same column width. The parent chooses columns and narrow-screen wrapping; media loading does not determine the frame heights.

<ComponentExample name="grid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/cadence/aspect-ratio";

export function RatioGrid() {
  const image = "data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22 viewBox=%220 0 320 240%22%3E%3Crect width=%22320%22 height=%22240%22 fill=%22%23334155%22/%3E%3Ccircle cx=%22240%22 cy=%2264%22 r=%2228%22 fill=%22%23fbbf24%22/%3E%3Cpath d=%22M0 240V180L100 80L240 240ZM120 240L240 120L320 200V240Z%22 fill=%22%2394a3b8%22/%3E%3C/svg%3E";
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg grid-cols-1 items-start gap-4 sm:grid-cols-3">
      {[{ ratio: 4 / 3, label: "4 : 3" }, { ratio: 1, label: "1 : 1" }, { ratio: 3 / 4, label: "3 : 4" }].map(({ ratio, label }) => (
        <figure key={label} className="grid gap-2">
          <AspectRatio ratio={ratio} className="overflow-hidden rounded-md">
            <img src={image} alt="Illustrated mountains and sun" className="size-full object-cover" />
          </AspectRatio>
          <figcaption className="text-center text-xs text-muted-foreground">{label}</figcaption>
        </figure>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- An image, video, or embed whose intrinsic size is unknown until it loads.
- A thumbnail grid that must not reflow as the images arrive.
- A placeholder that will be replaced by media of a known shape.

## When not to use

- Fixed-size icons or avatars; give them a size and be done.
- Text blocks. A ratio box around text clips exactly the content that needs to grow.
- A container whose height should follow its content — that is a normal block.

## API

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                            |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ratio`     | `number` | –       | Width ÷ height. Required — there is no sensible default. |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last; `overflow-hidden` and the radius go here.  |

The ratio is written as `--ratio`, and the box uses `aspect-(--ratio)`. Your own
`style` is preserved: the custom property is merged after it.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The whole point of the box is that it does not change size; a
transition here would reintroduce the layout shift it exists to prevent.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- The box is a layout element with no role. Put the meaning on the media: a real
  `alt` on images, a `title` on iframes.
- A background-only ratio box (no media yet) is decorative — keep it empty, or give
  it `aria-hidden` if it would otherwise be an empty accessible node.
- Media that animates (autoplay video, GIF) counts against both the CLS budget and
  the reduced-motion contract; pause or replace it under
  `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Responsiveness and performance

The frame derives height from its available width and ratio. Give it a constrained parent and size
media to fill the frame; the caller owns breakpoint-specific ratios and image loading.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not
imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for
this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Always pass a `ratio`; `16 / 9` for video, `1` for avatars, `4 / 3` for photos.
- Put `object-cover` on the child, not on the ratio box. The box only reserves
  space; the child fills it.

# Avatar

People in comments, assignees, and member lists.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/avatar
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarImage } from "@/components/cadence/avatar";

export function Author() {
  return (
    <Avatar>
      <AvatarImage src="/ada.png" alt="Ada Lovelace" />
      <AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback>
    </Avatar>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

`size` sets `data-size` on each root. Small, default and large are 24, 32 and 40 CSS pixels; children follow their own root rather than a shared page setting.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import {
  Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage,
} from "@/components/cadence/avatar";

export function AvatarSizes() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      {(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => (
        <Avatar key={size} size={size} aria-label={`Ada Lovelace, ${size}`}>
          <AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback>
        </Avatar>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Image and fallback

Always include a fallback. The first avatar shows initials while its image loads, then the image replaces them. The second deliberately supplies invalid image bytes to demonstrate an error; the third has no image at all. Base UI owns this loading state and swaps content without a cross-fade.

<ComponentExample name="image-fallback" />

```tsx
import {
  Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage,
} from "@/components/cadence/avatar";

export function AvatarImageAndFallback() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-6">
      <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-2 text-sm">
        <Avatar aria-label="shadcn">
          <AvatarImage src="https://github.com/shadcn.png" alt="shadcn" />
          <AvatarFallback>SC</AvatarFallback>
        </Avatar>
        <span>Image</span>
      </div>
      <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-2 text-sm">
        <Avatar aria-label="Grace Hopper">
          <AvatarImage src="data:image/png;base64,invalid" alt="Grace Hopper" />
          <AvatarFallback>GH</AvatarFallback>
        </Avatar>
        <span>Failed image</span>
      </div>
      <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-2 text-sm">
        <Avatar aria-label="Ada Lovelace">
          <AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback>
        </Avatar>
        <span>No image</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Presence

A badge is static presence feedback, not a loading pulse. Its dot follows the root size; a supplied icon is hidden at the smallest size. Keep a text alternative even when the icon disappears.

<ComponentExample name="presence" />

```tsx
import { CheckIcon } from "lucide-react";
import {
  Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage,
} from "@/components/cadence/avatar";

export function AvatarPresence() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      {(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => (
        <Avatar key={size} size={size} aria-label={`Ada Lovelace, ${size}`}>
          <AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback>
          <AvatarBadge>
            <CheckIcon aria-hidden="true" />
            <span className="sr-only">Online</span>
          </AvatarBadge>
        </Avatar>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Group

Group overlaps a short list and leaves overflow counting to the caller. Give all members of a group the same size; the count tile follows that group. These three independent groups show the supported sizes without linking their state.

<ComponentExample name="group" />

```tsx
import {
  Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount, AvatarImage,
} from "@/components/cadence/avatar";

export function AvatarGroups() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-6">
      {(["sm", "default", "lg"] as const).map((size) => (
        <AvatarGroup key={size} aria-label={`Reviewers, ${size}`}>
          <Avatar size={size} aria-label="Ada Lovelace"><AvatarFallback>AL</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
          <Avatar size={size} aria-label="Grace Hopper"><AvatarFallback>GH</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
          <Avatar size={size} aria-label="Katherine Johnson"><AvatarFallback>KJ</AvatarFallback></Avatar>
          <AvatarGroupCount aria-label="3 more reviewers">+3</AvatarGroupCount>
        </AvatarGroup>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- A person or an entity next to content they own: a comment, an assignee, a commit.
- A stack of participants, with a `+3` tile for the rest.
- A presence indicator on a collaborator, via `AvatarBadge`.

## When not to use

- A logo that must stay legible at small sizes; use the image with a fixed box.
- A decorative illustration; avatars imply a person or an account.
- More than about five faces. Past that the stack stops being readable — use
  `AvatarGroupCount` with a name list in the tooltip.

## API

| Part               | Props                        | Notes                                                        |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Avatar`           | `size`, Base UI root props   | `size`: `"default" \| "sm" \| "lg"`. Sets `data-size`.        |
| `AvatarImage`      | Base UI image props          | `src`, `alt`. Hidden automatically when the image fails.      |
| `AvatarFallback`   | Base UI fallback props       | Rendered while loading and after an error.                    |
| `AvatarBadge`      | native span props            | Corner dot; sized from the root's `data-size`.                |
| `AvatarGroup`      | native div props             | Overlapping stack with a ring in the page colour.             |
| `AvatarGroupCount` | native div props             | The `+3` tile that closes a stack.                            |

All parts carry `data-slot`, so `[&>[data-slot=avatar]]:size-6` style overrides are
possible without a prop.

Root, Image and Fallback accept Base UI state callbacks for `className` and `style`.
Caller classes merge last; Badge and group parts use native string classes and object styles.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The image-to-fallback swap is instant by design: Base UI knows when
the image errored, and a cross-fade would show a half-drawn face in the meantime.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Accessibility

- `AvatarImage` is an `<img>`: always pass a real `alt`. With a name beside the
  avatar, use `alt=""` so it is not announced twice.
- `AvatarFallback` prints initials. Those initials are the accessible name when the
  image is missing, so derive them from the person's actual name.
- `AvatarBadge` is a visual dot. Give it a text alternative when the presence state
  matters — e.g. `<span className="sr-only">Online</span>` inside it, or an
  `aria-label` on the badge.
- An avatar that links to a profile must be wrapped in an `<a>` with an accessible
  name; the image `alt` alone is not a link name.

## Responsiveness and performance

Avatar sizes are explicit rather than breakpoint-driven. Groups overlap avatars; the caller limits
the visible count and supplies overflow text. Base UI owns image loading and fallback state after
hydration.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Always render an `AvatarFallback`; without it a failed image leaves an empty hole.
- Do not animate the presence dot. State lives in the DOM (`aria-label`, text), not
  in a pulse.

# Skeleton

Placeholders while cards, tables, and lists load.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/skeleton
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/cadence/skeleton";

export function CardPlaceholder() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-3" aria-busy="true" aria-live="polite">
      <Skeleton className="h-40 w-full rounded-xl" />
      <Skeleton className="h-4 w-2/3" />
      <Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Text lines

Match line lengths to the incoming paragraph and put the busy state on the containing region. These blocks are decorative and do not receive focus.

<ComponentExample name="text-lines" />

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/cadence/skeleton";

export function TextLines() {
  return (
```
