```tsx
  <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
  <AlertDialogDescription>Every deployment goes with it.</AlertDialogDescription>
</AlertDialogHeader>
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <AlertDialogContent>…</AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>;
```

## A confirmation that is still working

The component never owns a request. The caller passes the in-flight state, and the library keeps the
button a button:

```tsx
<AlertDialogAction disabled={isDeleting} onClick={() => mutate()}>
  {isDeleting ? "Deleting…" : "Delete project"}
</AlertDialogAction>
```

## When to use

- A destructive or irreversible action — deleting a project, revoking a key, overwriting a draft — that the
  user must confirm on purpose.
- A decision the page cannot make for the user: move the workspace, leave without saving, end the session.
- A step that must be acknowledged before anything else continues, where an accidental dismissal would be
  the bug.

## When not to use

- A task with more than one decision or a form to fill in. Use `dialog`: it can be dismissed, and it should be.
- A message that does not block anything. Use `alert` where it belongs on the page, or `toast` for a moment.
- A hint attached to a control. Use `tooltip`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AlertDialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete` | Base UI root. Always modal; pointer dismissal is fixed off. |
| `AlertDialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `AlertDialogContent` | `size` (`"default" \| "sm"`), `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `AlertDialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `AlertDialogContent`. |
| `AlertDialogHeader` / `AlertDialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `AlertDialogMedia` | `className` | Icon slot; changes the header layout. |
| `AlertDialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `AlertDialogDescription` | `className` | Supporting text; wire it to the decision, not the product. |
| `AlertDialogAction` | `variant`, `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Confirming Button. The caller owns closing via the root’s controlled `open` value. |
| `AlertDialogCancel` | `variant` (`outline`), `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Dismissing button. Also closes the dialog. |

`AlertDialogCancel` renders Base UI’s Close. `AlertDialogAction` matches the pinned upstream
Button: clicking it invokes the caller’s handler and leaves the popup open. Use controlled
`open` / `onOpenChange` to close when the caller decides the action is complete.

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (overlay 96ms, panel 132ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so no transition runs | – | – |

The entrance is the dialog's, because this is the same popup: a fade under a 0.96-scale settle. The
motion is CSS-only — Base UI toggles `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style` and the class list
reads the duration tokens — so there is no JavaScript animation loop and nothing to interrupt by hand.
Reopening during the exit reverses the fade rather than restarting it.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. Focus never reaches the page behind it. |
| Escape | Cancels: the dialog closes and focus returns to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused button — confirm or cancel, whichever has focus. |

The outside press is the one path that is deliberately missing: clicking the overlay does nothing,
which is the difference between this component and `dialog`.

## Accessibility

The destructive action uses foreground text on a tinted destructive background. This preserves the warning colour while meeting text contrast in both themes.

- Base UI provides `role="alertdialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and the Escape path.
- `AlertDialogTitle` is required: an alert dialog without an accessible name is invalid, and it is
  announced as the first thing inside the popup. `AlertDialogDescription` becomes the description, so
  put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph.
- Focus lands on the cancel control, the first tabbable element inside the popup, not on the destructive
  action — so a stray Enter cancels rather than confirms. Put `AlertDialogCancel` first in the footer for
  that reason; the footer's column-reverse layout still shows the confirming action on top.
- Destructive styling is colour plus a specific verb ("Delete project", not "OK"). Never rely on the
  red alone; the label has to carry the meaning in greyscale and in a screen reader.
- `AlertDialogMedia` is decorative when the title already says what happened. Mark the icon
  `aria-hidden="true"` unless it is the only signal.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred with a 1rem gutter on narrow viewports: `max-w-lg` for the default size and
`max-w-xs` for `size="sm"`. The footer stacks its buttons in reverse DOM order (the confirming action
on top) below `sm`, and becomes a row that ends on the right above it. With `size="sm"` the two
buttons split the width instead of stacking, so the two answers stay side by side at every size.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit transition.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `width`/`height` transition, and no
  JavaScript animation running while the dialog sits open.
- `AlertDialogAction` and `AlertDialogCancel` are ordinary `Button`s, so the press feedback is the
  button's (a 0.97 scale that the same motion mode can drop).

## Notes for AI

- Reach for `alert-dialog` only when the answer must be deliberate. A form, a longer task, or anything
  the user may want to dismiss belongs in `dialog`.
- Always render `AlertDialogTitle`; it is the accessible name. Use `AlertDialogDescription` for the
  consequence of the action, in one sentence.
- Name the confirming button after its effect ("Delete project", "Leave without saving"), never "OK".
- Cancel closes automatically. The confirming Action stays open; use the root’s controlled `open` value when the caller decides to close.
- Use `AlertDialogMedia` for an icon, not for an illustration: the slot is a 4rem square that changes
  the header layout.

# Popover

Filters, share links, and other controls tied to a trigger.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/popover
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function SharePopover() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Share</PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent>
        <PopoverHeader>
          <PopoverTitle>Share this project</PopoverTitle>
          <PopoverDescription>Anyone with the link can read it, nobody can edit it.</PopoverDescription>
        </PopoverHeader>
        <p className="text-sm">cadence.dev/p/cadence-ui</p>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

## Positioned by side

`side` and `align` choose the placement, and the panel flips when there is no room. The motion follows
the anchor, not the side: the panel grows from `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the
trigger.

```tsx
<PopoverContent side="top" align="start" sideOffset={8}>
  …
</PopoverContent>
```

## With a form

The panel is a normal container, so `Field` and `Input` work inside it. Nothing traps focus: a popover
is non-modal by default.

```tsx
<PopoverContent>
  <PopoverHeader>
    <PopoverTitle>Rename this view</PopoverTitle>
  </PopoverHeader>
  <Field>
    <FieldLabel htmlFor="view-name">Name</FieldLabel>
    <Input id="view-name" defaultValue="Open PRs" />
  </Field>
</PopoverContent>
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Popover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <PopoverContent>…</PopoverContent>
</Popover>;
```

## Modal when it has to be

A popover that holds a destructive control can trap focus and block the page behind it without becoming
a dialog:

```tsx
<Popover modal>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Danger zone</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>…</PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## When to use

- A small set of controls that belongs to the thing it is attached to: column visibility, a filter, a
  share link, a colour picker.
- Context that would crowd the page if it were always visible, but that the user opens on demand.
- An edit that is scoped to one trigger and can be dismissed without losing the page.

## When not to use

- A confirmation that must be answered. Use `alert-dialog`: a popover can be dismissed by clicking away.
- A task that needs the whole screen or a focus trap. Use `dialog` or `sheet`.
- A one- or two-word hint on a control. Use `tooltip`, which cannot hold interactive content.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Popover` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root. Non-modal by default. |
| `PopoverTrigger` | native button props, `render` | The anchor and the toggle. |
| `PopoverContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal and positioner; `sideOffset` defaults to `4`. |
| `PopoverHeader` | `className` | Stacked title and description. |
| `PopoverTitle` | `className` | Base UI heading; the panel's accessible name. |
| `PopoverDescription` | `className` | Muted supporting text; becomes `aria-describedby`. |

`PopoverContent` positions itself; there is no `PopoverAnchor` export, because Base UI anchors to the
trigger and upstream's Base UI surface has no anchor part.

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – |

The panel grows out of its anchor rather than sliding towards it. A slide would need a distance token
and four per-side classes, and it moves the edge the positioner just lined up away from the trigger;
`--transform-origin` says the same thing with one transform. The scale reads `--motion-scale-in`, so
the class list carries a token and not a number.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Opens the popover from its trigger. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the panel's controls and then out of it; focus is not trapped unless `modal`. |
| Escape | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. |

Pressing outside closes it, which is the difference between a popover and an alert dialog.

## Accessibility

- Base UI gives the popup `role="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` on the trigger, `aria-controls`, and focus
  return on close. The panel is labelled by `PopoverTitle` and described by `PopoverDescription` when
  both are rendered.
- The trigger keeps `aria-expanded` in step, so assistive technology announces "collapsed" / "expanded"
  rather than a dialog appearing out of nowhere.
- `PopoverTitle` is optional for an interactive panel, but any popover that opens a region of controls
  should have one: an unnamed dialog is announced as just "dialog".
- Interactive controls inside the panel are reachable: the popover is non-modal, so Tab leaves it and
  the trigger's focus ring stays where the user left it.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is `w-72` wide and flips sides when the trigger has no room above or below; Base UI also
shifts it along the cross axis to stay inside the viewport. On a narrow screen it can fill most of the
width — pass `className="w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]"` or a max width when the content is wider than the
default.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the portal unmounts after the exit transition.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript
  animation loop. Reopening during the exit reverses the fade.

## Notes for AI

- Use `popover` for anchored, dismissible content; use `alert-dialog` when the answer must be explicit.
- Pass the trigger through `render`, not a wrapper: the trigger is what the positioner anchors to and
  what gets `aria-expanded`.
- Do not simulate a modal confirmation with `modal`; it blocks outside interaction but still closes on
  Escape, which is not what a confirmation promises.

Popover resolves its local token clock inside the portal, including timeScale and
reducedDurationScale. Callback classes/styles are evaluated with Base UI state and
merged last. Live reduced removes scale transitions; none cancels transitions and
renders without hidden starting/ending opacity, including nested provider overrides.

# Tooltip

Hints for icon buttons, shortcuts, and truncated values.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/tooltip
```

Optionally wrap the app in `TooltipProvider` once to set one delay for every tooltip; Base UI does not
require it.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function BoldTooltip() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider delay={200}>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" />} aria-label="Bold">
          <Bold />
        </TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent>Bold (⌘B)</TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Side and alignment

`side` defaults to `top` and the label flips when there is no room. The arrow moves with it; the panel
grows out of `--transform-origin`, so the scale starts where the trigger meets the label.

```tsx
<TooltipContent side="right" align="start">
  Right, aligned to the start
</TooltipContent>
```

## A delay for the whole app

`TooltipProvider` sets the delay once. Without it, Base UI's own default applies.

```tsx
<TooltipProvider delay={300}>
  <App />
</TooltipProvider>
```

## Disabled controls

A disabled button does not emit pointer events, so wrap it and put the hint on the wrapper:

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={<span className="inline-flex" />}>
    <Button disabled>Deploy</Button>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>Finish the required fields first</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

## When to use

- An icon-only control whose meaning is not obvious from the icon alone.
- The full value behind a truncated label, or a keyboard shortcut next to an action.
- A hint that helps the first use of a dense control and is useless once learned.

## When not to use

- Anything the user must read to act: a tooltip disappears on scroll, touch, and Escape. If the content
  matters, put it on the page or in a `popover`.
- Interactive content. A tooltip cannot hold a button or a link; use `popover`.
- The accessible name of a button that already has text. Two labels that disagree is worse than one.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TooltipProvider` | `delay` | Optional. One delay for every tooltip inside. |
| `Tooltip` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | Base UI root. |
| `TooltipTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Hover or focus target; carries `aria-describedby`. |
| `TooltipContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, popup, and arrow. `side` defaults to `top`, `sideOffset` to `4`. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | label `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | label `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the label appears on the first frame | – | – |

A tooltip is small enough that `duration.fast` is already at the edge of readable: nothing here waits
for an exit to finish. The arrow is part of the popup and moves with it, so it is never animated
separately.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focus shows the label; leaving hides it. |
| Escape | Hides the label and leaves focus on the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the trigger. The tooltip does not swallow the press. |

Hover alone is never the only path: the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too, which is what makes it
usable on touch and from a screen reader.

## Accessibility

- Base UI's own tooltip adds neither `role="tooltip"` nor `aria-describedby`; Cadence wires both. The
  trigger points at the popup only while it is open — a closed popup would otherwise leave a dangling
  id, which axe reports — and the popup is `role="tooltip"`.
- The tooltip must not be the only name of a control. Give an icon button a real `aria-label`; the
  tooltip is the extra sentence, not the name.
- Text stays readable in both themes: `bg-foreground` / `text-background` invert, so the label keeps
  contrast against whatever surface it floats over.
- Escape dismisses it without moving focus, so a tooltip never traps a keyboard user.

## Responsive behavior

The label is `w-fit` with a `max-w-xs` cap and wraps at word boundaries (`text-balance`) instead of
running off screen. Base UI flips the side and shifts the alignment when the viewport cannot fit it.

## Performance

- The popup tree is mounted only while the label is open; a page can carry dozens of tooltips without
  paying for them all.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no measuring loop, no JavaScript animation.
  Hover is not a state the component polls.

## Notes for AI

- Use a tooltip to name or explain a control, never to deliver information the user needs to proceed.
- Do not put a link, button, or form inside it; use `popover`.
- Give every icon-only trigger an `aria-label`: the tooltip complements the name, it does not replace it.

# Hover Card

Previews of links, profiles, and repositories.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/hover-card
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card";

export function ReviewerCard() {
  return (
    <p>
      Reviewed by{" "}
      <HoverCard>
        <HoverCardTrigger render={<a href="/u/linruoxin" />}>@linruoxin</HoverCardTrigger>
        <HoverCardContent>
          <p className="text-sm font-medium">Lin Ruoxin</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Maintains the motion layer and the registry.</p>
        </HoverCardContent>
      </HoverCard>
    </p>
  );
}
```

## With an action inside

The card is not modal and does not trap focus, so a link or a button inside it works normally. Base UI
keeps the card open while the pointer or focus is inside it, which is what makes the action reachable.

```tsx
<HoverCardContent>
  <p className="text-sm font-medium">Lin Ruoxin</p>
  <Button size="xs" variant="secondary">
    Follow
  </Button>
</HoverCardContent>
```

## Placement

`side` defaults to `bottom` — unlike a tooltip, which defaults to `top` — because the card is larger and
reads better below the link. `alignOffset` defaults to `4` for the same reason.

```tsx
<HoverCardContent side="right" align="start">
  …
</HoverCardContent>
```

## Trigger delay

`HoverCardTrigger` owns `delay` and `closeDelay`, defaulting to 600ms and 300ms in the installed Base UI. The root owns open state.

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger delay={400} closeDelay={300} render={<a href="/profile" />}>Profile</HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent>Profile preview</HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>
```

## When to use

- A preview of what a link leads to: a profile, a repository, a document — enough to decide whether to
  click.
- Context that helps a name make sense — the person behind an `@handle`, the project behind a package.
- A short panel with one or two actions that should not interrupt the page.

## When not to use

- A label for an icon. Use `tooltip`: it is smaller, quicker, and announced as a description.
- Content the user opened on purpose. Use `popover`: hover cards close when the pointer moves on, and
  anything with a task in it deserves a deliberate open.
- Information the user needs to answer a question. Nothing that appears and disappears on hover can be
  the only place it lives.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HoverCard` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | Base UI root; owns open state. |
| `HoverCardTrigger` | native anchor props, `render`, `delay`, `closeDelay` | The link or button the card describes. |
| `HoverCardContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, and popup. `side` defaults to `bottom`, `sideOffset` to `4`, `alignOffset` to `4`. |

The portal renders `data-slot="hover-card-portal"`; the popup is `data-slot="hover-card-content"`. There
is no `HoverCardArrow`: upstream's Base UI surface has none, and the card is a surface rather than a
pointer.

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – |

Same anchored motion as `popover` and `tooltip`: the scale starts at `--transform-origin`, which Base UI
points at the trigger. Hover cards close when the pointer leaves, so the exit has to be short; `fast` is
the anchored-surface duration the three share.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the trigger opens the card; moving focus into it keeps it open. |
| Escape | Closes the card and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Follows the trigger link, or activates a control inside the card. |

Keyboard focus opens the card for the same reason it does in a tooltip: without it, the content would
exist only for pointer users.

## Accessibility

- The trigger carries the accessible name; the card is supplementary. That is why Cadence does not give
  the popup `role="dialog"` or wire it as the trigger's description: a panel that may hold several
  paragraphs and a button is neither a name nor a description, and a screen reader reading it on every
  focus would be noise.
- Interactive content inside the card is reachable in order: Tab moves from the trigger into the card's
  links and buttons, and the card stays open while focus is inside it.
- Hover is never the only path: focus opens it too, and Escape closes it, so the card never traps a
  keyboard user.
- If the card is the only place a piece of information exists, it is in the wrong component — move it
  into the page or into a `popover`.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is `w-64` with `p-4`; Base UI flips it to another side and shifts the alignment when the
viewport cannot fit it. On touch devices there is no hover: the trigger still opens the card on focus or
tap, and the content must not assume a pointer is nearby.

## Performance

- Mounted only while open, so a page of links carries no extra popup trees.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript
  animation loop. The card follows the anchor through the positioner, not through React state.

## Notes for AI

- Use `hover-card` only for a preview of the linked thing; use `popover` for anything the user opens to
  act, and `tooltip` for a label.
- The trigger must have its own text or `aria-label`; the card is not its name.
- Keep the card small: a person, a repository, a document summary, one action. If it needs scrolling, it
  wants to be a `popover` or a page.

# Sheet

Filters, details, and settings that keep the page in view.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/sheet
```

This also installs `button`, which the sheet uses for its close control and its footer actions.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/sheet";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function FiltersSheet() {
  return (
    <Sheet>
      <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Open filters</SheetTrigger>
      <SheetContent>
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle>
          <SheetDescription>Applied to this view only. Nothing is saved.</SheetDescription>
        </SheetHeader>
        {/* the filter controls */}
        <SheetFooter>
          <SheetClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Reset</SheetClose>
          <SheetClose render={<Button />}>Apply filters</SheetClose>
        </SheetFooter>
      </SheetContent>
    </Sheet>
  );
}
```

## The four edges

`side` is `"right"` by default; the panel takes its placement classes and its slide direction from it.

```tsx
<SheetContent side="left">…</SheetContent>
<SheetContent side="top">…</SheetContent>
<SheetContent side="bottom">…</SheetContent>
```

## Without the built-in close button

The close button is a real control with a screen-reader-only label. Drop it when the footer already
carries an obvious way out, but keep one of the two.

```tsx
<SheetContent showCloseButton={false}>…</SheetContent>
```

## A long list

The panel is a flex column, so a scroll container goes around the part that overflows rather than on
the close button's positioning context:

```tsx
<SheetContent>
  <SheetHeader>…</SheetHeader>
  <div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-4">…</div>
  <SheetFooter>…</SheetFooter>
</SheetContent>
```

## Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <SheetContent>…</SheetContent>
</Sheet>;
```

## When to use

- A task that should keep the page in view: filters, a details panel, settings for the thing behind it.
- A form too tall or too wide for a `popover`, opened on purpose and dismissed on purpose.
- Mobile navigation or a secondary menu, where a full dialog would feel heavy.

## When not to use

- A confirmation that must be answered before anything continues. Use `alert-dialog`.
- A hint about a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`.
- A flow with its own steps and URL. That is a page, not an overlay.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Sheet` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI dialog root. |
| `SheetTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the sheet. |
| `SheetContent` | `side` (`"right" \| "left" \| "top" \| "bottom"`), `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `SheetOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `SheetContent`. |
| `SheetPortal` | `container` | Available for a custom portal target. |
| `SheetClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the sheet. |
| `SheetHeader` / `SheetFooter` | `className` | Padding and stacking only. |
| `SheetTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `SheetDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `translate` from its own size; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.base` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `translate` back off its edge; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no translate; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (132ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel is in place on the first frame | – | – |

The slide is `translate-*-full`, the panel's own width or height, not a fixed distance: a side panel
should enter from off its edge at every size, and a distance token would need one value per side. The
transition list names `translate` rather than `transform` because Tailwind v4's `translate-*` utilities
write the property individually — the same reason the dialogs transition `scale`.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the sheet; focus never reaches the page behind it. |
| Escape | Closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

The panel and backdrop resolve local token clocks from the effective mode and time scale, including
full inside a parent none scope. None also removes starting/ending opacity classes, so no hidden
starting frame remains. Caller state callback classes/styles still merge last.

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- `SheetTitle` is required: a sheet without an accessible name is invalid. `SheetDescription` becomes
  the description, so put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph.
- The built-in close control is a button with a screen-reader-only "Close" label; it sits in the
  top-right corner at every side and never traps the focus ring.
- A destructive footer action uses `variant="destructive"` plus a specific verb; the colour is never the
  only signal.

## Responsive behavior

A right or left sheet is `w-3/4` capped at `sm:max-w-sm`; a top or bottom sheet spans the width with an
auto height. Long content should scroll inside a wrapper (see "A long list"), so the footer stays
reachable and the page behind does not move.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit.
- Animates `opacity` and `translate` only: the panel is `fixed` at its edge, so nothing reflows and the
  page behind never reads layout.
- The close control is a `Button`, so its press feedback obeys the same motion mode as the sheet.

## Notes for AI

- Use `sheet` for a task beside the page; use `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate, and
  `popover` when the content is small and anchored to a control.
- Always render `SheetTitle`; put the side effect of closing (reset, discard) in the footer, not in the
  title.
- Name the footer action after its effect ("Apply filters"), not "OK".
- If the sheet opens a form, remember P11: the sheet renders invalid state from `aria-invalid` but never
  validates anything itself.

# Drawer

Quick tasks on touch screens, such as share or move.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/drawer
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/drawer";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function MoveConversation() {
  return (
    <Drawer showSwipeHandle>
      <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Move conversation</DrawerTrigger>
      <DrawerContent>
        <DrawerHeader>
          <DrawerTitle>Move conversation</DrawerTitle>
          <DrawerDescription>Drag down to dismiss, or pick a destination.</DrawerDescription>
        </DrawerHeader>
        {/* the destinations */}
        <DrawerFooter>
          <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DrawerClose>
        </DrawerFooter>
      </DrawerContent>
    </Drawer>
  );
}
```

## A visible swipe handle

`showSwipeHandle` draws the handle that says "drag me". It is `aria-hidden`: the drag is an accelerator,
never the only way out — the close controls and Escape still work.

```tsx
<Drawer showSwipeHandle>…</Drawer>
```

## Swiping from another edge

`swipeDirection` moves the sheet, its placement, and the direction it closes in. The default is `"down"`.

```tsx
<Drawer swipeDirection="right">…</Drawer>
<Drawer swipeDirection="up">…</Drawer>
```

## Snap points

`snapPoints` lets the sheet rest at more than one height; the peek is the smallest value. The overlay
stays in step with the swipe, so the page behind returns as the sheet travels.

```tsx
<Drawer snapPoints={[0.5, 1]}>…</Drawer>
```

## Non-modal

A drawer that should not lock the page passes `modal={false}`; the backdrop is skipped and the page
stays interactive.

```tsx
<Drawer modal={false}>…</Drawer>
```

## When to use

- A short task opened from the bottom of the screen, where the thumb is: move to, share, quick actions.
- A list or explanation that the page behind should stay visible for — a bottom sheet covers the bottom,
  not the context.
- A panel the user expects to swipe away, because that is how sheets behave on touch devices.

## When not to use

- A decision that must be answered. Use `alert-dialog`; a drawer can be dragged shut.
- A hint on a control. Use `tooltip` or `hover-card`.
- A long multi-step flow. Use a page or a `sheet` with a footer; dragging half-way through a form is a
  worse experience than a full surface.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Drawer` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`, `snapPoints`, `swipeDirection`, `showSwipeHandle` | `showSwipeHandle` is additive; `swipeDirection` defaults to `"down"` and `modal` to `true`. |
| `DrawerTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the drawer. |
| `DrawerContent` | `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay (when modal), viewport, popup, and content. |
| `DrawerOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DrawerContent`. |
| `DrawerSwipeHandle` | `className` | The handle; rendered for you when `showSwipeHandle` is set. |
| `DrawerClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the drawer. |
| `DrawerHeader` / `DrawerFooter` | `className` | Stacking and spacing only. |
| `DrawerTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DrawerDescription` | `className` | Supporting text. |

## Motion contract

Each portal surface resolves its own mode and token clock. A nested full scope restores timing inside none (subject to the system preference). Live reduced cancels scale or slide and keeps opacity; none cancels transitions and shows the first frame immediately. Base parts accept `className(state)` and `style(state)`; caller values merge last.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | sheet `opacity 0 → 1` + `transform` from `--closed-transform`; backdrop `opacity 0 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| drag | `transform` follows `--drawer-swipe-movement-*`; backdrop opacity is `1 - --drawer-swipe-progress` | Base UI gesture (no authored recipe) | yes (it is the gesture) |
| exit | sheet back to `--closed-transform` + `opacity → 0`; backdrop `opacity → 0` | `exit.fade` · `duration.slow` / `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | fade only: the closed-state slide is dropped, so the sheet appears and disappears in place | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the sheet is in place on the first frame | – | – |

The drag keeps tracking the finger under `reduced`: that movement is the user's own, not authored motion,
and a sheet that ignored the drag would be worse than one that follows it. The release animation uses the
token duration rather than a velocity-scaled one — the swipe physics decide *where* the sheet settles,
the token decides how long the settle takes.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside a modal drawer. |
| Escape | Closes the drawer and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling while the drawer is modal.
- `DrawerTitle` is required: a drawer without an accessible name is invalid.
- The swipe handle is `aria-hidden="true"` and is never the only way out. A user who cannot drag gets
  the close controls, Escape, and the overlay press (for a modal drawer).
- The content region scrolls on its own (`overflow-y-auto`), so a long list inside the sheet does not
  move the page behind it.

## Responsive behavior

The default sheet sits at the bottom, spans the width, and caps its height at `calc(100dvh - 3rem)` so a
strip of the page stays visible. `swipeDirection="left"` / `"right"` becomes a side panel at `w-3/4`,
capped at `max-w-sm` from `sm` up. Snap points change the resting height without changing any of that
geometry.

## Performance

- The drag writes CSS variables and a `transform`; it never touches layout or React state per frame.
- The backdrop opacity is a `calc()` on the same variable, so the page behind dims as the sheet moves
  without a second animation.
- Entry and exit animate `transform` and `opacity` only. Nothing is measured during render.

## Notes for AI

- Use `drawer` for a short touch-first task from the bottom edge; use `sheet` for a side panel that
  holds a form, and `alert-dialog` when the answer must be deliberate.
- Always render `DrawerTitle`. `DrawerDescription` is the second line of the announcement.
- Never make the swipe the only dismissal: keep a `DrawerClose`, and let Escape work.
- For a list of actions, each row is a `DrawerClose` so choosing one closes the sheet.

# Select

Choosing one value from a short list of options.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/select
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "@/components/cadence/select";

export function FrameworkSelect() {
  return (
    <Select defaultValue="next">
      <SelectTrigger className="w-48" aria-label="Framework">
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="next">Next.js</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="remix">Remix</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="astro">Astro</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

The default trigger is for forms; `size="sm"` fits dense rows. The empty control uses a placeholder without adding an empty option. Each select owns its value.

<ComponentExample name="sizes" />

```tsx
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function Sizes() {
  return <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3"><FrameworkSelect /><FrameworkSelect size="sm" /><FrameworkSelect empty /></div>;
}
```

## Groups and labels

`SelectGroup` and `SelectLabel` name related options; `SelectSeparator` separates groups. Orange is disabled while keyboard navigation can still reach Carrot.

<ComponentExample name="groups" />

```tsx
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectItem, SelectLabel, SelectSeparator, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

export function Groups() {
  return (
    <Select items={[{ value: "apple", label: "Apple" }, { value: "orange", label: "Orange" }, { value: "carrot", label: "Carrot" }]} defaultValue="apple">
      <SelectTrigger aria-label="Produce"><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectGroup>
          <SelectLabel>Fruits</SelectLabel>
          <SelectItem value="apple">Apple</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem value="orange" disabled>Orange</SelectItem>
        </SelectGroup>
        <SelectSeparator />
        <SelectGroup>
          <SelectLabel>Vegetables</SelectLabel>
          <SelectItem value="carrot">Carrot</SelectItem>
        </SelectGroup>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}
```

## Controlled value

The caller owns `value` and `onValueChange`. The external action chooses Astro in this example only; selections in other cards stay independent.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function Controlled() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>("next");
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        <Select items={frameworks} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
          <SelectTrigger aria-label="Controlled framework"><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent>{frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}</SelectContent>
        </Select>
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setValue("astro")}>Choose Astro externally</Button>
      </div>
      <output className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">Value: {value}</output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Form submission

`name` supplies the hidden input for FormData. `required` delegates empty-value checks to the browser; select a framework, then submit to read the caller-owned result.

<ComponentExample name="form-submission" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function FormSubmission() {
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState<string>();
  return (
    <form className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3" onSubmit={(event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
      setSubmitted(String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("framework")));
    }}>
      <Select items={frameworks} name="framework" required>
        <SelectTrigger aria-label="Framework to submit"><SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" /></SelectTrigger>
        <SelectContent>{frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}</SelectContent>
      </Select>
      <Button type="submit">Submit framework</Button>
      <output className="w-full text-sm" aria-live="polite">{submitted ? `Submitted: ${submitted}` : "No submission yet"}</output>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Disabled and invalid

Disabled prevents selection. Invalid is a supplied visual and accessible state, with an independently identified error; the caller decides when to clear it.

<ComponentExample name="disabled-invalid" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

function FrameworkSelect({ size = "default", empty = false }: { size?: "default" | "sm"; empty?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue={empty ? undefined : "next"}>
      <SelectTrigger size={size} aria-label={empty ? "Framework, empty" : size === "sm" ? "Framework, small" : "Framework"}>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}

export function DisabledInvalid() {
  const errorId = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        <Select items={frameworks} disabled defaultValue="next">
          <SelectTrigger aria-label="Framework, disabled"><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent><SelectItem value="next">Next.js</SelectItem></SelectContent>
        </Select>
        <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue="astro">
          <SelectTrigger aria-label="Framework, invalid" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby={errorId}><SelectValue /></SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent>{frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>{label}</SelectItem>)}</SelectContent>
        </Select>
      </div>
      <p id={errorId} className="text-sm text-destructive">This framework is unavailable for your project.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Multiple values

`multiple` keeps an array of values and leaves the list open while options are toggled. The trigger lists the selected labels; Escape closes the list and restores focus. Use Combobox for a searchable multi-select or chips.

<ComponentExample name="multiple" />

```tsx
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

export function Multiple() {
  return (
    <Select items={frameworks} multiple defaultValue={["next", "astro"]}>
      <SelectTrigger aria-label="Multiple frameworks">
        <SelectValue placeholder="Choose frameworks" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => (
          <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
            {label}
          </SelectItem>
        ))}
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  );
}
```

## Panel placement

The first row fixes the four sides; the second fixes start, center and end alignment. These examples disable `alignItemWithTrigger` so the popup uses the requested anchored placement instead of overlaying the selected item. Viewport collision handling may flip the effective side. Each trigger keeps its own value and associated label.

<ComponentExample name="placement" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "@/components/cadence/select";

const frameworks = [
  { value: "next", label: "Next.js" },
  { value: "remix", label: "Remix" },
  { value: "astro", label: "Astro" },
];

export function Placement() {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="flex w-full flex-col items-center gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        {(["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const).map((side) => (
          <div key={side} className="grid gap-2">
            <label htmlFor={`${id}-${side}`} className="text-xs capitalize">
              {side} panel
            </label>
            <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue="next">
              <SelectTrigger id={`${id}-${side}`} aria-label={`Framework, ${side} panel`}>
                <SelectValue />
              </SelectTrigger>
              <SelectContent side={side} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
                {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => (
                  <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
                    {label}
                  </SelectItem>
                ))}
              </SelectContent>
            </Select>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-3">
        {(["start", "center", "end"] as const).map((align) => (
          <div key={align} className="grid gap-2">
            <label htmlFor={`${id}-${align}`} className="text-xs capitalize">
              {align} alignment
            </label>
            <Select items={frameworks} defaultValue="next">
              <SelectTrigger id={`${id}-${align}`} aria-label={`Framework, ${align} alignment`}>
                <SelectValue />
              </SelectTrigger>
              <SelectContent align={align} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
                {frameworks.map(({ value, label }) => (
                  <SelectItem key={value} value={value}>
                    {label}
                  </SelectItem>
                ))}
              </SelectContent>
            </Select>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Choosing one value from a list that is too long for radios but too short to need search.
- A compact form control where the current value should stay visible in the trigger.
- A setting that changes the surface around it, so the value and its width should move together.

## When not to use

- Free-text or type-to-filter input. Use `combobox` once it ships, or an `input` with a datalist.
- Two or three mutually exclusive options that should stay visible. Use `radio-group`.
- Navigation between routes. Use a menu or links; a select submits a value, it does not navigate.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Select` | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `disabled`, `required`, `name`, `multiple`, `items` | Base UI root; `items` lets `SelectValue` render labels from data. |
| `SelectTrigger` | `size` (`"sm" \| "default"`), native button props | Contains `SelectValue`; the chevron is rendered for you. |
| `SelectValue` | `placeholder` | The selected label, or the placeholder when empty. |
| `SelectContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `alignItemWithTrigger` | Portals, positions, and sizes to `--anchor-width`. |
| `SelectItem` | `value`, `disabled` | Renders the label and the check indicator. |
| `SelectGroup` / `SelectLabel` | group props | Purely structural. |
| `SelectSeparator` | separator props | A single hairline. |
| `SelectScrollUpButton` / `SelectScrollDownButton` | scroll-arrow props | Appear only when the list overflows. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pointer selection | value slot width | `geometry.resize` | yes (physics-defined, clamped) |
| pointer selection | label `x`/`y` from the item to the trigger | `handoff` | yes |
| pointer selection | check `scale` / `opacity` | `state.morph` | yes |
| open / close | popup `opacity` / `scale` | `popup.anchored` | yes |
| reduced | width jumps, no flight, no scale; opacity stays | – | – |
| none | every duration is zero | – | – |

The trigger's label is laid out at its final width inside a clipped slot. Animating that slot's width
folds the surface without re-wrapping the label. The portalled label follows the live destination
as the trigger resizes, including shifts in centered or right-aligned rows, so the flight and real
label meet at the same position. Keyboard selection has no origin, so it changes the width and lets the label swap
without a flight; the pointer keeps the spatial handoff.
The portalled flight label uses its natural text width, so a longer selection stays fully visible
even if Base UI has not yet committed the destination label when its position is measured.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The site header changes the inherited motion mode on the same component tree, including each named example. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive. A cancelled selection
does not fly the pointer label over the current value. Natural text width is observed
separately from the animated outer slot, including content and viewport changes.

## Keyboard interactions

- `Enter` / `Space` / `ArrowDown` opens the list and focuses the selected item.
- `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` moves the highlight; `Home` / `End` jump to the ends.
- Typeahead letters move the highlight to the next matching label.
- `Enter` selects; `Escape` closes without changing the value.
- `Tab` closes the list and moves focus to the next control.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders the trigger as a combobox and the popup as a listbox, wired with
  `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-activedescendant`.
- Name the control with `aria-label` or a visible external label associated with the trigger; the value alone is not a name.
- The selected item keeps `aria-selected="true"`; the check is a visual duplicate, not the only signal.
- Under reduced motion the value still changes and the check still appears; nothing is conveyed by
  the flight alone.
- The handoff clone is `aria-hidden`: screen readers hear the value once, from the trigger.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns selection values, validation, error text, submission and any remote
loading/filtering. Render supplied aria-invalid/data-invalid and associate described
errors; this component does not validate or install a form-state library.

## Responsive behavior

The popup is at least `--anchor-width` wide and caps at `--available-height`, so it flips and scrolls
inside the viewport. `alignItemWithTrigger` keeps the selected item over the trigger on touch, where a
list attached below the finger is harder to read. The width animation is short and only touches the
trigger, so a select in a toolbar does not reflow the page beyond its own row.

## Performance

- One measured width animation and, on pointer selection, one absolutely positioned label for the
  duration of the handoff. No blur and no shadow animation.
- Width is a layout property; it is allowed only on this T3 component and only through
  `geometry.resize`, which jumps under reduced and none.
- The list virtualisation is Base UI's; the component adds no per-item animation beyond the check
  indicator.
- Budget: T3 (12 KB gzip). If a page animates several selects at once, only the open one moves.

## Notes for AI

- Prefer `SelectValue placeholder="…"` over an empty first item; an empty item is a selectable value.
- Keep item labels short and distinct; typeahead matches their text.
- Do not add a separate "selected" class to the trigger; the value already carries the state.
- For invalid state, pass `aria-invalid`; the trigger styles it from the attribute.

# Combobox

Picking from a long list you can filter by typing.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/combobox
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxInput,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxList,
} from "@/components/cadence/combobox";

const frameworks = ["Next.js", "SvelteKit", "Nuxt.js", "Remix", "Astro"];

export function FrameworkPicker() {
  return (
    <Combobox items={frameworks}>
      <ComboboxInput placeholder="Select a framework" aria-label="Framework" />
      <ComboboxContent>
        <ComboboxEmpty>No framework found.</ComboboxEmpty>
        <ComboboxList>
          {(item) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
              {item}
            </ComboboxItem>
          )}
        </ComboboxList>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

`ComboboxList` takes a render function, so the list is data, not markup: `items` on the root is what the
popup filters and what the render callback receives.

## Groups and separators

Long catalogues read better in labelled groups. Give each `ComboboxGroup` its own `items` so filtering
can drop a group as a whole.

```tsx
<Combobox items={groups}>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Assign reviewer" aria-label="Reviewer" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No reviewer found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(group) => (
        <ComboboxGroup key={group.value} items={group.items}>
          <ComboboxLabel>{group.value}</ComboboxLabel>
          {group.items.map((item) => (
            <ComboboxItem key={item.value} value={item}>
              {item.label}
            </ComboboxItem>
          ))}
        </ComboboxGroup>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Clear and trigger controls

`showClear` adds the undo affordance once a value is set; the chevron steps aside while both would be
fighting for the same 24px. Turn the chevron off entirely with `showTrigger={false}` when the field is
inside a form that submits on Enter.

```tsx
<Combobox items={frameworks} defaultValue="Astro">
  <ComboboxInput showClear placeholder="Select a framework" aria-label="Framework" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
          {item}
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>
```

## Multiple values

`multiple` turns the field into a tag editor: `ComboboxChips` is the frame, each `ComboboxChip` is a
value, and `ComboboxChipsInput` is the caret. Anchor the popup to the chips container so it lines up with
the field rather than with the input inside it.

```tsx
const anchor = useComboboxAnchor();

<Combobox multiple items={topics} defaultValue={["design"]}>
  <ComboboxChips ref={anchor}>
    <ComboboxValue>
      {(value: string[]) => (
        <React.Fragment>
          {value.map((topic) => (
            <ComboboxChip key={topic}>{topic}</ComboboxChip>
          ))}
          <ComboboxChipsInput placeholder="Add topic" aria-label="Topics" />
        </React.Fragment>
      )}
    </ComboboxValue>
  </ComboboxChips>
  <ComboboxContent anchor={anchor}>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No topic found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
          {item}
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>;
```

## Filtering a server list

For a remote catalogue, keep the list the server returned and hand it to `items`; Base UI filters what it
is given, so a new response replaces the list without the component deciding what to fetch.

```tsx
const [results, setResults] = useState<string[]>([]);

<Combobox items={results} onInputValueChange={(query) => search(query).then(setResults)}>
  <ComboboxInput placeholder="Search a city" aria-label="City" />
  <ComboboxContent>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No city found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => (
        <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>
          {item}
        </ComboboxItem>
      )}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>;
```

## When to use

- Choosing one value from a list too long to scan: countries, assignees, repositories.
- A search field that should also accept a typed value, for example a tag the catalogue does not list.
- Several values from the same catalogue, where each choice should stay visible as a chip.
- A picker whose options arrive from a search endpoint rather than from a constant.

## When not to use

- Fewer than about eight fixed options. Use `select`; a popup that has to be opened to show three items is
  slower than three radios.
- Commands rather than values — navigation, actions, "go to file". Use `command`.
- Free text with no catalogue behind it. Use `input`.
- A control that must not accept typing, such as a language picker in a settings form. Use `select`.

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Combobox` | `items`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `multiple`, `disabled`, `name`, `required`, `onInputValueChange`, `itemToStringLabel` | Base UI root. `items` drives what the popup filters and what the render callbacks receive. |
| `ComboboxInput` | `showTrigger` (`true`), `showClear` (`false`), `disabled`, native input props | The field: a bare input inside an input-group frame, with the chevron and the optional clear button. |
| `ComboboxTrigger` | native button props | The chevron on its own, for a field built by hand. |
| `ComboboxValue` | render callback or children | The selected label; in the chips layout it renders the chips. |
| `ComboboxContent` | `side` (`"bottom"`), `sideOffset` (`6`), `align` (`"start"`), `alignOffset` (`0`), `anchor` | Portals, positions, and sizes to `--anchor-width`. |
| `ComboboxList` | children or render function `(item, index) => ReactNode` | Scrolls, and takes the height the popup has left. |
| `ComboboxItem` | `value`, `disabled` | Renders the label and the tick. |
| `ComboboxGroup` / `ComboboxLabel` | `items` on the group | Structural; the group's `items` let filtering drop it whole. |
| `ComboboxEmpty` | children | Shown when the filter matches nothing. |
| `ComboboxSeparator` | separator props | A hairline between unrelated groups. |
| `ComboboxChips` / `ComboboxChip` / `ComboboxChipsInput` | `showRemove` (`true`) on the chip | The multi-value layout. |
| `ComboboxCollection` | collection props | Escape hatch for virtualised lists. |
| `useComboboxAnchor` | – | A ref to anchor the popup to the chips frame. |

`ComboboxClear` is internal on purpose: it belongs to `ComboboxInput`'s layout, and a component that owns
an undo affordance should not also hand out half of one.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | popup `opacity` 0→1, `scale` `--motion-scale-in`→1 | `popup.anchored` | yes: a CSS transition, so reopening reverses it |
| close | popup `opacity` 1→0 | `exit.fade` | yes |
| select | tick `scale` `0.96`→1, `opacity` 0→1 | `state.morph` | yes: a spring, retargeted from the current value |
| filter | none — rows are replaced, not moved | – | – |
| reduced | popup fades without scaling, tick appears at full size | – | – |
| none | every duration is zero | – | – |

The scale grows out of `--transform-origin`, which Base UI writes from the positioner, so the panel opens
from the field rather than from its own centre. The list itself never animates: a filter runs on every
keystroke, and a row that is still travelling when the next character arrives is a list the reader has to
chase.

Each portal resolves token durations from its local provider, including `full` nested inside
`none` (the OS reduced-motion preference still wins). Full → reduced cancels running panel
geometry and keeps the opacity transition; `none` cancels opacity too and is visible on the
first mounted frame. The preview's **Popup motion** selector changes the local mode on the
same component tree. Base UI `className(state)` and `style(state)` callbacks are evaluated
before merging; caller utilities and styles win. Native `render`, events and ref cleanup
remain owned by the primitive. Base UI 1.9's typeable focus manager hides background
nodes from assistive technology while leaving their tab stops enabled. Cadence adds native
temporary negative tab indices only to newly hidden focus stops, preserving outside pointer activation; Tab releases them before normal focus navigation and
Base UI's blur dismissal. Existing hidden/inert nodes and parent dialogs keep their owners; cleanup preserves caller tabindex changes. `ComboboxInput` string classes style the field frame;
state callback classes style the native input with its real Base UI input state.

## Keyboard interactions

- `ArrowDown` or `Alt+ArrowDown` opens the popup; with it open, `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the highlight.
- Typing filters the list and moves the highlight to the first match.
- `Enter` selects the highlighted item and closes the popup.
- `Escape` closes the popup without choosing anything; the typed query stays in the field.
- `Tab` closes the popup and moves focus to the next control.
- `Backspace` in the chips layout deletes the last chip when the input is empty.

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders the input as a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and
  `aria-activedescendant`, and the list as a `listbox` whose rows are `option`s.
- Name the field: `aria-label` on `ComboboxInput`, or a `Field`/`Label` pair around it. The placeholder is
  not a name.
- The selected row keeps `aria-selected="true"`; the tick is a visual duplicate, never the only signal.
- The empty state is a row inside the list, so it is reachable in the reading order and not a modal
  interruption.
- Under reduced motion nothing is conveyed by the panel's scale: the list is there, the tick is at full
  size, and `aria-selected` carries the state.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns selection values, validation, error text, submission and any remote
loading/filtering. Render supplied aria-invalid/data-invalid and associate described
errors; this component does not validate or install a form-state library.

## Responsive behavior

The popup is exactly `--anchor-width` wide and at least `--spacing(7)` wider than the field, so a narrow
trigger still shows a readable row. It flips above the field near the viewport edge, and the list — not the
popup — scrolls inside `--available-height`. In the chips layout the frame wraps to a second line instead
of scrolling horizontally, and the popup widens to the chips container.

## Performance

- One CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale` per open and per close; no JS animation loop, and no layout
  read.
- One spring per selected row. The indicator is mounted once and animated in place, so filtering does not
  create and destroy an animation per item.
- The filter is synchronous over whatever `items` holds; a remote list is a debounce in the caller, not a
  behaviour of this component.
- Budget: T2 (10 KB gzip).

## Notes for AI

- Always pass `items` to `Combobox`; it drives filtering and is what the `ComboboxList` render callback
  receives. Without it the list renders nothing.
- Use `value`/`onValueChange` for a controlled picker, `defaultValue` otherwise — same contract as `select`.
- `multiple` requires the chips layout; do not pair `multiple` with a plain `ComboboxInput`.
- Do not add a "loading" prop: async feedback is the caller's state, and `ComboboxEmpty` is for an empty
  result, not for a pending one.
- For invalid state pass `aria-invalid` on `ComboboxInput`; the frame styles the border and the ring from
  the attribute.

# Dropdown Menu

Row actions, filters, and view settings behind one button.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dropdown-menu
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dropdown-menu";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function RowActions() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuContent align="start">
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => rename()}>Rename</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => duplicate()}>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

## Items, shortcuts, and destructive actions

An item is a `menuitem`: it runs, then the menu closes. `DropdownMenuShortcut` is a
right-aligned hint only — the component binds no keys, so register the shortcut yourself.
`variant="destructive"` colours the label and its icons; `inset` indents an item to line up
with one that has a check mark.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => edit()}>
  Edit
  <DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘E</DropdownMenuShortcut>
</DropdownMenuItem>
<DropdownMenuSeparator />
<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => remove()}>
  Delete
  <DropdownMenuShortcut>⌘⌫</DropdownMenuShortcut>
</DropdownMenuItem>
```

## Checkbox and radio items

Both keep the menu open, so a user can set several options in one visit. The mark is the
item's state, not a second control: `aria-checked` carries it for assistive technology, and
the mark scales in as confirmation.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuCheckboxItem defaultChecked onCheckedChange={setDescription}>
  Description
</DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>

<DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={density} onValueChange={setDensity}>
  <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="compact">Compact</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
  <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="comfortable">Comfortable</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
</DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
```

## Submenus

A submenu is a menu anchored to its trigger item. It opens on hover after the pointer rests,
on `ArrowRight`, and on click; `DropdownMenuSubContent` takes the same placement props as the
top-level panel, with `side="right"` as the default.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuSub>
  <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Move to</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuSubContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => move("backlog")}>Backlog</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => move("review")}>In review</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuSubContent>
</DropdownMenuSub>
```

## Grouping

`DropdownMenuGroup` binds a `DropdownMenuLabel` to the items it holds: the group is labelled
by it, so a screen reader announces "Pull request, group". A label outside a group is a
plain caption above the items, which is what most toolbars want.

```tsx
<DropdownMenuGroup>
  <DropdownMenuLabel>Pull request</DropdownMenuLabel>
  <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => edit()}>Edit</DropdownMenuItem>
  <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => duplicate()}>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
</DropdownMenuGroup>
```

## Controlled open

`open` and `onOpenChange` make the menu controlled, which is how a menu is opened from
outside its trigger — a keyboard shortcut, a row's context, a tour step.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<DropdownMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Actions</DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent>…</DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>;
```

## When to use

- A row of actions behind one trigger: a table row, a card, a file.
- A filter or view setting where the panel stays open while several options change.
- A command list too long for a toolbar and too short to need search.

## When not to use

- A list of links to another page. Use a `navigation-menu` or plain links: an item that
  navigates is a link, and a menu item is not one.
- A value you select and read back. Use `select`, which keeps the chosen value in the trigger.
- A destructive answer that must be confirmed. Use `alert-dialog`; a menu item is a
  one-keystroke action and closes immediately.
- More than about a dozen entries, or entries the user has to search. Use `command`.

## API

### `DropdownMenu`

| Prop           | Type                       | Default | Description                                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                  | –       | Controlled open state.                          |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                  | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state.                     |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`  | –       | Fires on every open and close, including Escape. |
| `modal`        | `boolean`                  | `true`  | Traps focus and makes the page inert while open. |

### `DropdownMenuTrigger`

Native button props and `render`. The trigger owns `aria-haspopup="menu"` and
`aria-expanded`; pass a `Button` through `render` rather than wrapping one, so those land on
the element the user presses.

### `DropdownMenuContent`

| Prop          | Type                                          | Default    | Description                                    |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right"`      | `"bottom"` | Preferred side; flips when there is no room.   |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                 | `"start"`  | Alignment along the trigger's edge.            |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                      | `4`        | Gap between trigger and panel, in pixels.       |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                      | `0`        | Shift along the alignment axis.                 |
| `className`   | string or Base UI state callback                                      | –          | Merged last.                                    |

### `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`

| Part                     | Props                                                              | Notes                                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `DropdownMenuItem`       | `onClick`, `disabled`, `inset`, `variant`, `closeOnClick`            | `variant`: `"default" \| "destructive"`.          |
| `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `inset`            | Keeps the menu open.                              |
| `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`                            | One selection for the group.                      |
| `DropdownMenuRadioItem`  | `value` (required), `disabled`, `inset`                             | Keeps the menu open.                              |
| `DropdownMenuSub`        | –                                                                  | Groups a submenu trigger and its content.         |
| `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` | `disabled`, `inset`                                                | Renders the chevron.                              |
| `DropdownMenuSubContent` | Same as `DropdownMenuContent`                                      | `side="right"`, `alignOffset={-3}` by default.    |

### `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`

`DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`,
`DropdownMenuShortcut`, `DropdownMenuPortal`.

## Motion contract

| Phase         | Properties                                        | Token             | Interruptible                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| open          | panel `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` from the trigger origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| close         | panel `opacity → 0`, `scale → 0.96`               | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes                |
| check / radio | mark `opacity` + `scale`                          | `state.morph`     | yes                          |
| reduced       | panel fades, no scale; the mark cross-fades at full size | `exit.fade` | yes                         |
| none          | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`; the mark jumps | –      | –                            |

Opening and closing are one CSS transition on `opacity` and `scale`, driven by Base UI's
`data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style`, so an interrupted close reverses rather than
restarts. The panel grows out of `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the trigger;
a submenu grows out of its item the same way, because both levels render the same panel.

The highlighted row is a colour change, not motion: `data-highlighted` switches the item's
background. A travelling highlight would be a shared element across items — `layout.move`,
