
## When to use

- Peer views of the same project.
- Settings categories that share a local context.
- Editors with preview and history panels.

## When not to use

- Use links and Breadcrumb for separate destinations.
- Use Accordion for sections that can remain open together.
- Use ToggleGroup for a set of independent formatting actions.

## API

### `Tabs`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | Base UI tab value | uncontrolled / `0` | Controlled or initial selection; null means none. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details) => void` | — | Change request with reason, activation direction and cancellation. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal` / `vertical` | `horizontal` | Layout and keyboard axis. |
| `className`, `style`, `render`, `ref` | Base UI Root props | — | Forwarded, including state callbacks. |

### `TabsList`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default` / `line` | `default` | Filled surface or edge indicator. |
| `activateOnFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Select on arrow focus. |
| `loopFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Wrap focus at either end. |

All Base UI List props pass through. `tabsListVariants` is exported for composing styles.

### `TabsTrigger`

`value` identifies the corresponding panel. `disabled` defaults to false. All Base UI Tab props pass
through, including `nativeButton`, `render`, `ref`, events and state-based classes/styles. User classes
merge last. The added `tabs-indicator` slot is decorative and aria-hidden.

### `TabsContent`

`value` links to the corresponding trigger. `keepMounted` defaults to false. All Base UI Panel props,
render/ref and state callbacks remain available. Panels switch immediately without size or entrance motion.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selection | Shared indicator transform via FLIP | `layout.shared`, physics-defined `spring.morph` | Yes, inherits velocity |
| Initial selection | Static indicator at selected trigger | — | — |
| Reduced | Static indicator, no layout/transform | No motion | Instant |
| None | Static indicator, no transform or animation | Zero duration | Instant |

Each list has a unique LayoutGroup. Default and line indicators follow both axes; independent and nested
lists cannot exchange indicators. The primitive owns active state, cancellation, disabled fallback and
mounting. Reduced and none render a plain span with no layoutId. Parent size changes leave the indicator
anchored to the selected trigger. There is no panel fade, height animation or extra recipe.

## Accessibility

Base UI provides tablist/tab/tabpanel roles, linked IDs and roving focus. Supply a list label. Selection
is exposed through aria-selected; focus remains on the operated tab. Disabled tabs remain arrow-focusable for discoverability but cannot activate. A custom
render must preserve supplied semantics, refs and children. Persistent hidden panels leave the focus order.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left / Right | Move horizontal tab focus; direction follows the surrounding DirectionProvider. |
| Up / Down | Move vertical tab focus. |
| Home / End | Focus the first / last enabled tab. |
| Enter / Space | Select the focused tab in default manual activation mode. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Leave the list for the panel or surrounding page. |

## Responsive behavior

No breakpoint changes selection or orientation. The caller chooses layout and may constrain or scroll
long lists. The indicator is inset within its active trigger and follows changes in label and parent size.

## Performance

T3 source budget: 12 KB gzip. Only the active indicator participates in shared layout projection;
there are no measurement observers or animation timers in this component. Server output includes the
initial selected indicator; initial=false avoids an entrance replay. Keep large lists and panels small.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve all five exports and the four upstream slots.
- Use value/defaultValue, not the retired animated-tabs items API.
- Keep each list scoped and preserve the explicit reduced/none static branch.
- Related: Accordion, Collapsible, ToggleGroup.

# Table

Invoices, transaction histories, and small collections of structured records.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/table
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell,
  TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow,
} from "@/components/cadence/table";

export function Invoices() {
  return (
    <Table tabIndex={0} className="focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring">
      <TableCaption>Recent invoices.</TableCaption>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="col">Invoice</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">Amount</TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        <TableRow>
          <TableCell>INV-001</TableCell>
          <TableCell className="text-right">$250.00</TableCell>
        </TableRow>
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

## Footer totals

`TableFooter` renders a native `tfoot`. Spans and numeric alignment are caller-owned.

```tsx
<TableFooter>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell colSpan={3}>Total</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right tabular-nums">$750.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
</TableFooter>
```

## Selected rows

Selection state belongs to the application. A data attribute supplies the visual
state; add a named checkbox when selection must be interactive. Setting this
attribute alone does not make a row a control or announce selection.

```tsx
<TableRow data-state="selected">
  <TableCell>INV-001</TableCell>
  <TableCell>Paid</TableCell>
</TableRow>
```

## When to use

- Invoice summaries with amounts and payment states.
- Transaction histories with a few consistent columns.
- Small record collections where column comparisons matter.

## When not to use

- For page layout: use CSS grid or flex.
- For large collections needing sorting, filtering, pagination, or virtualization:
  compose those behaviours in the application; Table only supplies markup and styles.
- For independent summaries with no column relationships: use cards or a list.

## API

All eight exports accept `React.ComponentProps` for their native element,
including `children`, `className`, `style`, event handlers, ARIA attributes and
React 19 `ref`. Classes merge last. No custom props or defaults are added.

| Export | Element |
| --- | --- |
| `Table` | `table` |
| `TableHeader` | `thead` |
| `TableBody` | `tbody` |
| `TableFooter` | `tfoot` |
| `TableRow` | `tr` |
| `TableHead` | `th` |
| `TableCell` | `td` |
| `TableCaption` | `caption` |

Each part's slot is its kebab-case name: `table`, `table-header`, `table-body`,
`table-footer`, `table-row`, `table-head`, `table-cell`, and `table-caption`.

`Table` also creates a `div` with `data-slot="table-container"` and
`relative w-full overflow-x-auto`. Its props, classes and ref target the **table**,
not that wrapper. Size the surrounding layout to constrain the scrolling region.
`TableHead` and `TableCell` keep upstream's no-wrap and checkbox alignment styles.
Rows retain hover, `data-state="selected"` and descendant `aria-expanded` feedback.

## Motion contract

T0: no motion recipe, hook, provider, or animation runtime. All modes render the
same static table. Row colour feedback is the upstream CSS colour transition;
rows do not enter, reorder, resize, or animate selection.

| Mode | Animated properties |
| --- | --- |
| full | none |
| reduced | none |
| none | none |

No timing token or interruption lifecycle applies.

## Accessibility

- Native table, row, header, cell and caption semantics remain intact. Provide a
  meaningful caption or an accessible name and use `scope` for header relationships.
- Static rows and cells stay out of the tab order. Links, buttons and checkboxes
  inside cells keep their native keyboard interaction; no grid arrow-key model is added.
- The wrapper scrolls horizontally on narrow screens; columns are not removed.
  If keyboard scrolling needs an explicit focus stop across your target browsers,
  pass `tabIndex={0}` to the named table with a visible focus ring, as in Usage.
  This supplies a focusable descendant of the scrolling container; arrow keys
  can scroll that ancestor without adding grid keyboard semantics.
- No layout measurement or data processing runs. Render large datasets through
  application-owned pagination or virtualization; the server markup remains native HTML.

## Responsiveness and performance

The table fills its container, which provides native horizontal scrolling when columns need more
width. The caller owns column sizing, wrapping and any sticky behavior. Rows are all rendered; large
datasets need application pagination or virtualization.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive
children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not
imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for
this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve the table hierarchy: caption, header, body and footer belong inside Table.
- Class names and refs on Table address the table; constrain its parent for overflow.
- Table does not fetch data, validate values, sort, filter, paginate or own selection.
- Do not add decorative row entrance or reorder motion to this T0 component.

# Carousel

A swipeable collection with previous and next controls.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/carousel
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Carousel aria-label="Featured projects" className="mx-12 max-w-sm" tabIndex={0}>
      <CarouselContent className="touch-pan-y">
        {[1, 2, 3].map((slide) => (
          <CarouselItem key={slide} aria-label={`${slide} of 3`}>
            <div className="rounded-lg border p-8">Project {slide}</div>
          </CarouselItem>
        ))}
      </CarouselContent>
      <CarouselPrevious />
      <CarouselNext />
    </Carousel>
  );
}
```

## Multiple visible slides

```tsx
<Carousel aria-label="Projects" opts={{ align: "start", loop: true }}>
  <CarouselContent className="-ml-2 touch-pan-y">
    {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((slide) => (
      <CarouselItem key={slide} className="pl-2 md:basis-1/2">
        Project {slide}
      </CarouselItem>
    ))}
  </CarouselContent>
  <CarouselPrevious />
  <CarouselNext />
</Carousel>
```

## Vertical collection

```tsx
<Carousel orientation="vertical" aria-label="Updates" className="my-12">
  <CarouselContent className="h-64 touch-pan-x">
    <CarouselItem>First update</CarouselItem>
    <CarouselItem>Second update</CarouselItem>
  </CarouselContent>
  <CarouselPrevious />
  <CarouselNext />
</Carousel>
```

## API and plugins

```tsx
"use client";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Carousel, type CarouselApi, CarouselContent, CarouselItem } from "@/components/cadence/carousel";

export function WithApi() {
  const [api, setApi] = useState<CarouselApi>();
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!api) return;
    const update = () => setSelected(api.selectedScrollSnap());
    update();
    api.on("select", update);
    return () => { api.off("select", update); };
  }, [api]);
  return (
    <>
      <Carousel setApi={setApi} aria-label="Projects">
        <CarouselContent>
          <CarouselItem>First</CarouselItem>
          <CarouselItem>Second</CarouselItem>
        </CarouselContent>
      </Carousel>
      <button onClick={() => api?.scrollNext()}>Next project</button>
      <p aria-live="polite">Project {selected + 1}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

Pass Embla plugins through `plugins`; keep plugin instances stable. The API is the actual Embla
8.6.0 instance, including events, `reInit`, `plugins`, `scrollTo`, `scrollProgress` and `destroy`.
Plugins are never removed by a motion mode. Stop autoplay or independent animation plugins under
reduced/none yourself, and provide pause controls. Cadence clamps the engine's interpolation even
when a plugin or API call explicitly requests `jump=false`.

## When to use

- Browse a short collection of related projects, cards or photos.
- Show one highlighted item with explicit previous/next navigation.
- Allow touch swiping alongside keyboard and button navigation.

## When not to use

- Use Tabs for named views that must remain directly selectable.
- Use Scroll Area for continuous reading or long lists.
- Keep essential content discoverable without relying on automatic advance.

## API

| Part | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Root | Native div props/ref; `orientation="horizontal"` (or `vertical`); `opts` and `plugins` use Embla types; `setApi(api)` receives the public instance. |
| Track | Native div props/ref/style/classes target the **inner track**. Its fixed overflow-hidden outer viewport owns the `carousel-content` slot and Embla ref. |
| Slide | Native div props/ref; group/slide semantics. Default full basis; caller classes size each slide. |
| Previous / Next | All Button props, including render, ref, state callback classes/styles and events. Defaults: outline, icon-sm. Caller disabled/onClick override the navigation defaults as upstream does. |
| Context hook | Context with API, viewport ref, original options, orientation, navigation functions and canScroll states. Throws outside Carousel. |
| API type | Exported Embla instance type (possibly undefined before initialization). |

The fixed Base UI API and new-york-v4 visuals are pinned at `96da9cc7f1aa`.
Navigation buttons retain the Base API's icon-sm default with the visual source's round size-8
shape. Orientation controls the axis even if opts.axis differs, as upstream does. Options such
as startIndex, align, loop, dragFree, watchDrag, breakpoints and direction pass to Embla.
For RTL set both native `dir="rtl"` and `opts.direction="rtl"`.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Recipe | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter / exit | — | No authored entrance or removal animation. |
| Interaction | `data.transition` | `data.transition`, engine form: Embla alone translates the track. Default duration.base maps to 22 attraction units via carouselClock; timeScale scales it. Explicit full-mode opts.duration remains native. |
| Interruption | — | Next/previous/drag retarget Embla's existing location and velocity. Release uses the effective base clock, including breakpoint options, instead of a hard-coded release duration. |
| Reduced | — | Track and loop relocation transforms retain the correct state position. Direct dragging remains available. All autonomous engine interpolation is zero; no CSS/Motion transform animation is added. |
| None | — | Same immediate state positioning, with every engine duration zero even for explicit API/plugin duration requests. |
| Buttons | — | Composed Button owns its declared feedback.press recipe; reduced/none remove press scale. Static control placement/vertical rotation are layout. |

A mode downgrade settles the existing target without resetting selection. Engine friction,
geometry and momentum destinations remain Embla-owned. Independent plugin animations remain
caller-owned. Removing the track transform would display the wrong slide and is not reduction.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Reach native controls and any focusable slide content. |
| Enter / Space | Activate a focused navigation button. |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Previous / next from inside the region, on both orientations (pinned upstream behaviour). |

Supply a region label and per-slide labels, and optionally a polite status as in the preview.
The root is not focusable by default; use tabIndex and a visible focus class when desired.
Embla scrolls focused offscreen slide content into view. Caller onKeyDownCapture replaces the
upstream capture handler; caller onClick similarly replaces the navigation action. This is not
a tab widget and does not hide offscreen content from assistive technology. Avoid interactive
content whose arrow handling conflicts with the root capture handler.

## Responsiveness and performance

Size slides with basis utilities and pair inner negative margins with slide padding. Vertical
tracks require an explicit height. Set touch-pan-y on horizontal tracks and touch-pan-x on
vertical tracks to preserve cross-axis page scrolling. Leave room for controls outside the viewport.
Embla observes viewport/slide geometry and slide mutations, reinitializing snaps as needed;
options/plugins reinitialize through the native React adapter. No layout reads happen in render.
SSR renders static first-slide markup, then Embla initializes after hydration. No autoplay,
virtualization or per-slide Motion instances are bundled. Only track transforms animate.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve opts, plugins, setApi, useCarousel and all native part props when adapting examples.
- Use the exposed Embla API for selection rather than applying another transform to the track.
- Keep selected position under reduced/none; assert the lack of interpolation, not transform:none.
- Use Button for individual actions, Tabs for directly named panels, and Scroll Area for long content.

# Scroll Area

Constrained lists and wide content with native scrolling and custom scrollbars.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/scroll-area
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@/components/cadence/scroll-area";

export function Notes() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea aria-label="Release notes" className="h-48 w-full rounded-md border">
      <ul className="flex flex-col gap-3 p-4 pr-6">
        {Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => <li key={i}>Release {i + 1}</li>)}
      </ul>
    </ScrollArea>
  );
}
```

## Horizontal scrolling

Add a horizontal ScrollBar inside ScrollArea and let content exceed the viewport width.
The built-in vertical scrollbar only appears when vertical overflow exists.

```tsx
<ScrollArea aria-label="Project timeline" className="w-full rounded-md border">
  <div className="flex w-max gap-4 p-4 pb-6">
    {["Research", "Design", "Build", "Review", "Ship"].map((phase) => (
      <div key={phase} className="w-40">{phase}</div>
    ))}
  </div>
  <ScrollBar orientation="horizontal" />
</ScrollArea>
```

## Caller rendering and sizing

Root props and ref belong to the outer container, not the inner scrolling viewport.
A custom render element must forward its props, children and ref. State callbacks
for classes and styles remain supported. Reserve space around content for overlaid tracks.

```tsx
<ScrollArea
  ref={rootRef}
  render={<section />}
  aria-label="Activity"
  className={(state) => state.hasOverflowY ? "h-48 rounded-md border" : "max-h-48"}
  style={{ maxWidth: "100%" }}
>
  <div className="p-4 pr-6">{activity}</div>
</ScrollArea>
```

## When to use

- Long activity feeds constrained by a panel height.
- Horizontal timelines or collections wider than their available space.
- Bounded lists that need custom scrollbars while retaining native scrolling.

## When not to use

- For ordinary page content: allow the document to scroll.
- For paged slides: use Carousel.
- For reading progress or smooth scrolling effects: this component adds neither.

## API

| Export | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `ScrollArea` | Base UI `ScrollArea.Root.Props`; no additional defaults. |
| `ScrollBar` | Base UI `ScrollArea.Scrollbar.Props`; `orientation="vertical"`, `keepMounted=false`. |

Both exports forward native events, ARIA, style, ref and Base UI `render`.
Classes merge last, including state callback classes. Root also forwards
`overflowEdgeThreshold` (Base UI default zero). Scrollbar props target the track;
the thumb is created internally. Root creates the viewport, default vertical track
and corner. ScrollArea's `children` render inside the viewport, including any
additional horizontal track, matching the pinned upstream composition.

Slots: `scroll-area`, `scroll-area-viewport`, `scroll-area-scrollbar`,
`scroll-area-thumb`. The scrollbar includes `data-orientation`.
Root classes, padding, borders and styles remain on the root; content padding
belongs on a child. Root ref does not address the viewport. No viewport prop or
ref API is invented; query its slot from the root for application-owned imperative scrolling.

## Motion contract

T0: empty recipe set, no provider, hook, timing token or authored animation.
Enter, exit and resize are immediate. Full, reduced and none share static markup.
The primitive positions and sizes its thumb from actual native scroll geometry;
those transforms represent user position and remain functional in every mode.
No smoothing, automatic scrolling, entrance or opacity transition is added.

| Mode | Authored motion |
| --- | --- |
| full | none |
| reduced | none |
| none | none |

Upstream focus-ring and colour feedback remain CSS state feedback. Native wheel,
touch momentum and keyboard scrolling follow browser/platform preferences.
Caller-added smooth scrolling and CSS animation are application-owned.

## Accessibility

- Base UI supplies a focusable viewport when overflow exists with a visible keyboard focus ring.
  Tab enters the viewport and its interactive descendants; arrows, Page Up/Down,
  Home/End retain native browser scrolling. No custom keyboard model is added.
- Give the root a meaningful accessible name, as in Usage. Keep list or document
  semantics in the content and label interactive controls individually.
- Tracks and thumbs are pointer controls; keyboard users scroll the native viewport.
- Constrain height for vertical overflow and width for horizontal overflow. The
  viewport retains all content on narrow screens; size a grid parent with `min-w-0`.
- Base UI updates geometry on native scrolling and viewport resize. The pinned
  wrapper has no Content part: content-only growth may leave the thumb stale until
  a scroll or viewport resize occurs. Cadence preserves that upstream behaviour. It adds no
  measurement loop, data processing or virtualization. Paginate or virtualize large
  datasets in the application.

## Responsiveness and performance

Give the root explicit dimensions so its viewport can scroll; horizontal scrolling needs the
corresponding ScrollBar. Parent grids may need min-w-0. Base UI manages custom scrollbar interaction
while content uses native scrolling; it does not virtualize children.

T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native
HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction
works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped
source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Preserve root/viewport ownership, native scrolling and Base UI render/ref support.
- Add ScrollBar with horizontal orientation for wide content; its default stays vertical.
- Do not add decorative fading, smooth scrolling or animation to this T0 component.

# Chart

Responsive data charts with themed tooltips and legends.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/chart
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Bar, BarChart, XAxis } from "recharts";
import { ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent } from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = { visits: { label: "Visits", color: "var(--primary)" } };
const data = [
  { month: "Jan", visits: 186 },
  { month: "Feb", visits: 305 },
];

export function Example() {
  return (
    <ChartContainer role="group" config={config} className="min-h-48 w-full" aria-label="Monthly visits">
      <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
        <XAxis dataKey="month" />
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
        <Bar dataKey="visits" fill="var(--color-visits)" />
      </BarChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  );
}
```

## Bar chart

Use bars to compare categories. Each series shares labels and colours with the tooltip and legend; the data table preserves exact values without relying on colour.

<ComponentExample name="bar" />

```tsx
import { Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, XAxis } from "recharts";
import {
  ChartContainer,
  ChartLegend,
  ChartLegendContent,
  ChartTooltip,
  ChartTooltipContent,
} from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

export function BarExample() {
  const data = baseline;
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">Monthly visits · bar</figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group" config={config} className="h-64 w-full min-w-0" aria-label="Monthly visits, bar chart">
        <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
          <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
          <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
          <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
          <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent hideIcon={false} />} />
          <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} isAnimationActive />
          <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} isAnimationActive />
        </BarChart>
      </ChartContainer>
      <DataTable data={data} />
    </figure>
  );
}
```

## Line chart

A line emphasizes the trend across ordered months. The series and axis belong to Recharts; ChartContainer supplies theme and motion context.

<ComponentExample name="line" />

```tsx
import { Line, LineChart, XAxis } from "recharts";
import { ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent } from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

export function LineExample() {
  const data = baseline;
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">Monthly visits · line</figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group" config={config} className="h-64 w-full min-w-0" aria-label="Monthly visits, line chart">
        <LineChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
          <XAxis dataKey="month" />
          <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
          <Line dataKey="desktop" stroke="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive />
        </LineChart>
      </ChartContainer>
      <DataTable data={data} />
    </figure>
  );
}
```

## Area chart

An area adds a filled region under a trend. Keep the fill and outline distinguishable in both themes and use the table for exact values.

<ComponentExample name="area" />

```tsx
import { Area, AreaChart, XAxis } from "recharts";

];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>

          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
```

## Pie chart

A pie compares the Desktop contribution of each month. `nameKey="month"` gives the tooltip meaningful category names; the adjacent data table supplies exact values.

<ComponentExample name="pie" />

```tsx
import { Pie, PieChart } from "recharts";
import { ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent } from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

export function PieExample() {
  const data = baseline;
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">Monthly visits · pie</figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group" config={config} className="h-64 w-full min-w-0" aria-label="Monthly visits, pie chart">
        <PieChart accessibilityLayer>
          <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent nameKey="month" />} />
          <Pie data={data} dataKey="desktop" nameKey="month" fill="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive />
        </PieChart>
      </ChartContainer>
      <DataTable data={data} />
    </figure>
  );
}
```

## Legends and theme colours

ChartStyle scopes the config colour variables to each chart. The first legend uses config icons; the second fixes `hideIcon` to show a text-only legend. Light and dark theme mappings apply independently of neighbouring examples.

<ComponentExample name="legends" />

```tsx
import { MonitorIcon, SmartphoneIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, XAxis } from "recharts";
import {
  ChartContainer,
  ChartLegend,
  ChartLegendContent,
  ChartTooltip,
  ChartTooltipContent,
} from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

const themeConfig = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", icon: MonitorIcon, theme: { light: "var(--chart-1)", dark: "var(--chart-2)" } },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", icon: SmartphoneIcon, theme: { light: "var(--chart-3)", dark: "var(--chart-4)" } },
};
function ThemedChart({ hideLegendIcons = false }: { hideLegendIcons?: boolean }) {
  const data = baseline;
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">Monthly visits · bar</figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group" config={themeConfig} className="h-64 w-full min-w-0" aria-label="Monthly visits, bar chart">
        <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
          <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
          <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
          <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
          <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent hideIcon={hideLegendIcons} />} />
          <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} isAnimationActive animationDuration={5000} />
          <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} isAnimationActive animationBegin={5000} />
        </BarChart>
      </ChartContainer>
      <DataTable data={data} />
    </figure>
  );
}
export function Legends() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-6">
      <ThemedChart />
      <ThemedChart hideLegendIcons />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Tooltip indicators and formatting

Compare dot, line, dashed and hidden indicators directly. Each real tooltip starts at February and remains available from the chart keyboard surface. The last chart formats its heading and value rows; `hideLabel` removes the heading in the hidden-indicator example. A config icon takes precedence over a marker, and entries with `type="none"` are omitted.

<ComponentExample name="tooltips" />

```tsx
import { Bar, BarChart, XAxis } from "recharts";
import { ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent } from "@/components/cadence/chart";

const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

function TooltipExample({
  indicator = "dot",
  hidden = false,
  formatted = false,
}: {
  indicator?: "dot" | "line" | "dashed";
  hidden?: boolean;
  formatted?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <figure className="grid min-w-0 gap-2">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">
        {formatted ? "Formatted values" : hidden ? "Without an indicator or heading" : `${indicator} indicator`}
      </figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group"
        config={config}
        className="h-48 w-full min-w-0"
        aria-label={`Visits, ${formatted ? "formatted" : hidden ? "no indicator" : indicator} tooltip`}
      >
        <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={baseline}>
          <XAxis dataKey="month" />
          <ChartTooltip
            defaultIndex={1}
            active
            content={
              <ChartTooltipContent
                indicator={indicator}
                hideIndicator={hidden}
                hideLabel={hidden}
                labelFormatter={formatted ? (label) => `Month: ${label}` : undefined}
                formatter={
                  formatted
                    ? (value, name) => (
                        <span>
                          {name}: {Number(value).toLocaleString()} visits
                        </span>
                      )
                    : undefined
                }
              />
            }
          />
          <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" />
        </BarChart>
      </ChartContainer>
    </figure>
  );
}

export function Tooltips() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-6">
      <TooltipExample />
      <TooltipExample indicator="line" />
      <TooltipExample indicator="dashed" />
      <TooltipExample hidden />
      <TooltipExample formatted />
      <DataTable data={baseline} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Live data and motion ownership

Each Update action replaces only its own chart data. Recharts owns interpolation and the data model; Cadence owns the `data.transition` clock. The deliberately explicit series timing below cannot override the inherited clock. `isAnimationActive={false}` opts a series out. Reduced and none settle geometry immediately, including a running transition when the header mode changes. Custom shapes, nested controllers and independent CSS/WAAPI must honour the same modes. Tooltip position changes stay immediate.

<ComponentExample name="live-data" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Area, AreaChart, Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, Line, LineChart, Pie, PieChart, XAxis } from "recharts";
import {
  ChartConfig,
  ChartContainer,
  ChartLegend,
  ChartLegendContent,
  ChartTooltip,
  ChartTooltipContent,
} from "@/components/cadence/chart";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

type ChartKind = "bar" | "line" | "area" | "pie";
const config = {
  desktop: { label: "Desktop", color: "var(--foreground)" },
  mobile: { label: "Mobile", color: "var(--muted-foreground)" },
};
const baseline = [
  { month: "Jan", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "Mar", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "Apr", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
];

function DataTable({ data }: { data: typeof baseline }) {
  return (
    <details className="text-sm">
      <summary className="cursor-pointer">View data table</summary>
      <table className="mt-2 w-full text-left">
        <caption className="sr-only">Monthly visits</caption>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Month</th>
            <th scope="col">Desktop</th>
            <th scope="col">Mobile</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {data.map((row) => (
            <tr key={row.month}>
              <th scope="row">{row.month}</th>
              <td>{row.desktop}</td>
              <td>{row.mobile}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </details>
  );
}

function VisitChart({
  kind = "bar",
  data = baseline,
  chartConfig = config,
  hideLegendIcons = false,
}: {
  kind?: ChartKind;
  data?: typeof baseline;
  chartConfig?: ChartConfig;
  hideLegendIcons?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <figure className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-3">
      <figcaption className="text-sm font-medium">Monthly visits · {kind}</figcaption>
      <ChartContainer role="group" config={chartConfig} className="h-64 w-full min-w-0" aria-label={`Monthly visits, ${kind} chart`}>
        {kind === "bar" ? (
          <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
            <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
            <XAxis dataKey="month" tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
            <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent hideIcon={hideLegendIcons} />} />
            <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} isAnimationActive animationDuration={5000} />
            <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} isAnimationActive animationBegin={5000} />
          </BarChart>
        ) : kind === "line" ? (
          <LineChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
            <XAxis dataKey="month" />
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
            <Line dataKey="desktop" stroke="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive animationDuration={5000} />
          </LineChart>
        ) : kind === "area" ? (
          <AreaChart accessibilityLayer data={data}>
            <XAxis dataKey="month" />
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
            <Area dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-mobile)" stroke="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive />
          </AreaChart>
        ) : (
          <PieChart accessibilityLayer>
            <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent nameKey="month" />} />
            <Pie data={data} dataKey="desktop" nameKey="month" fill="var(--color-desktop)" isAnimationActive />
          </PieChart>
        )}
      </ChartContainer>
      <DataTable data={data} />
    </figure>
  );
}

function UpdatingChart({ kind }: { kind: ChartKind }) {
  const [updated, setUpdated] = useState(false);
  const data = updated
    ? baseline.map((row) => ({ ...row, desktop: 350 - row.desktop, mobile: row.mobile + 40 }))
    : baseline;
  return (
    <div className="grid min-w-0 gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" className="justify-self-start" onClick={() => setUpdated((value) => !value)}>
        Update {kind} data
      </Button>
      <output className="text-sm" aria-live="polite">
        {updated ? "Updated" : "Baseline"}
      </output>
      <VisitChart kind={kind} data={data} />
    </div>
  );
}

export function LiveData() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-8">
      <UpdatingChart kind="bar" />
      <UpdatingChart kind="line" />
      <UpdatingChart kind="area" />
      <UpdatingChart kind="pie" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Comparing categories with a bar chart.
- Showing trends with Recharts Line/Area series.
- Sharing labels, colours and formatting between series, tooltip and legend.

## When not to use

- Exact values without a visual comparison: use Table.
- A single completion value: use Progress.
- Large datasets requiring canvas/WebGL: choose a dedicated rendering engine.

## API

### `ChartContainer`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| config | ChartConfig | required | Per-series label, icon, color or light/dark theme. |
| children | ResponsiveContainer children | required | Recharts chart composition. |
| initialDimension | `{ width: number; height: number }` | 320 × 200 | Initial SSR/responsive fallback. |
| id | string | React useId | Scoped data-chart suffix; upstream does not forward id as a DOM id. |
| className / style / ref | div props | — | Applied to outer div; classes merged last. |

### `ChartTooltip` and `ChartTooltipContent`

ChartTooltip accepts Recharts Tooltip props; positional CSS animation is always disabled.
ChartTooltipContent retains upstream Recharts Tooltip, default content and div prop types.
Native div attributes, styles, events and refs apply to the content root. Engine placement and
animation metadata is not emitted as DOM attributes.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| indicator | dot / line / dashed | dot | Series marker. |
| hideLabel / hideIndicator | boolean | false | Suppress heading / marker. |
| nameKey / labelKey | string | — | Resolve config keys from payload. |
| formatter / labelFormatter | Recharts callbacks | — | Custom row / heading. |
| color / labelClassName / className | string | — | Marker / heading / root styles. |
| active / payload / label | Recharts content props | — | Usually injected by Tooltip. |

### `ChartLegend`, `ChartLegendContent`, `ChartStyle`, `ChartConfig`

ChartLegend is Recharts Legend. ChartLegendContent accepts default legend content + div prop
types; consumes className, payload, nameKey, hideIcon=false, verticalAlign="bottom". Top alignment
adds bottom padding. Native div attributes, styles, events and refs apply to the content root.
Legend formatter receives the resolved label, entry and index; onClick/onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave
receive entry, index and event. Clickable entries support Tab, Enter and Space. Engine placement
and animation options belong on ChartLegend/ChartTooltip. ChartStyle accepts id
and config and emits nothing without configured colours. ChartConfig is a record of label/icon
plus either color or a complete light/dark theme map. Helpers require ChartContainer context.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Series enter / data update | SVG data geometry (T4 engine form) | `data.transition` | Recharts retargets from its series state |
| Tooltip / legend | Immediate placement; no wrapper reveal | — | Immediate |
| Reduced | Geometry jumps to final data; no transform/scale tween | `data.transition` | Running controller completes |
| None | Zero animation duration; final data | `data.transition` | Running controller completes |

The full clock is duration.base / ease.out, scaled by provider timeScale. Reduced adds no fade
because comparison must remain legible. Static SVG coordinate transforms are retained in all
modes. This is not a DOM layout animation. Mode changes do not remount the chart.

## Accessibility

Give the chart an accessible name, keep Recharts accessibilityLayer enabled, and provide a
text summary or data table for exact values. Tooltips are supplemental. Labels and values must
convey meaning independently of colour. Use a visible focus ring on the chart surface when needed.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Enter / leave the Recharts chart surface. |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Move the active data point and tooltip in Cartesian charts. |

Legend content is descriptive, not a toggle control. Add native buttons for series filtering.

## Responsive behavior

Give ChartContainer a nonzero height or min-height. ResponsiveContainer measures available
space through ResizeObserver; the initialDimension fallback is 320 × 200. Use fewer ticks and
short labels on narrow screens; a caption and data table remain available without pointer input.

## Performance

Recharts is an explicit dependency, loaded only on chart pages in this site. Limit plotted data
and series rather than animating thousands of marks. Cadence uses one rAF per active series,
cancels on cleanup, and completes immediately in reduced/none. No render-time DOM measurement
or wrapper entrance is added. Browser evidence covers data updates, resize and mode downgrade.

## Notes for AI

Keep the upstream composition: ChartContainer wraps a Recharts chart; it does not accept data.
Import series and axes from Recharts. Never erase SVG coordinate transforms to satisfy a motion
assertion. Related: Table for values, Progress for one completion value, Calendar for dates.

# Calendar

Select dates, multiple days, and ranges with accessible month navigation.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/calendar
```

## Usage

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { Calendar } from "@/components/cadence/calendar";

export function Example() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>();
  return <Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />;
}
```

## Multiple dates

```tsx
const [days, setDays] = useState<Date[] | undefined>([]);
<Calendar mode="multiple" selected={days} onSelect={setDays} max={5} />;
```

## Date ranges

```tsx
import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker";
const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>();
<Calendar mode="range" selected={range} onSelect={setRange} min={2}
  disabled={{ dayOfWeek: [0, 6] }} excludeDisabled />;
```

## Localized navigation

```tsx
import { fr } from "date-fns/locale";
<Calendar locale={fr} weekStartsOn={1} captionLayout="dropdown"
  startMonth={new Date(2020, 0)} endMonth={new Date(2030, 11)} />;
```

## When to use

- Pick a date in a booking or scheduling interface.
- Select several independent days or a contiguous range.
- Browse adjacent months with keyboard and localized captions.

## When not to use

Use an Input for free-form date text. Compose a Popover for a date-picker field;
Calendar itself is an inline calendar, without field serialization or popup orchestration.

## API

### `Calendar`

All DayPicker 9.13.2 props and discriminated selection types are preserved.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mode | single / multiple / range | undefined | No selection when omitted. |
| selected / onSelect | DayPicker selection type / handler | — | Caller owns selected values. |
| month / onMonthChange | Date / handler | — | Controlled navigation. Otherwise use defaultMonth. |
| showOutsideDays | boolean | true | Show days from adjacent months. |
| captionLayout | DayPicker caption layout | label | Label or native month/year dropdowns. |
| buttonVariant | Button variant | ghost | Navigation button appearance. |
| locale / weekStartsOn | Partial Locale / 0–6 | DayPicker locale | Labels, formatting and week boundary. |
| disabled / hidden | Matcher or Matcher[] | — | DayPicker matching rules. |
| numberOfMonths / fixedWeeks / showWeekNumber | number / boolean / boolean | 1 / false / false | Grid layout options. |
| className / classNames / style / styles | DayPicker styles | — | Caller overrides win. |
| formatters / labels / components | DayPicker overrides | — | Override individual formatters, accessible labels or entire parts. |
| animate | boolean | false | Forwarded upstream API; external DayPicker animation CSS is caller-owned. Do not combine a second CSS clock with Cadence motion. |

### `CalendarDayButton`

Accepts DayPicker's DayButton props (`day`, `modifiers`, native button attributes) plus
`locale?: Partial<Locale>`. Preserves native events, disabled state, classes, styles and
focus management. Selection and range modifiers have the upstream data attributes.
Custom components replace default parts completely and must maintain the same accessibility
and motion contract. A custom Month or MonthGrid also takes ownership of month motion.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Month changes | opacity and signed horizontal transform on the actual grid | `data.transition`, distance.sm | Yes; latest month replaces the target, without remounting the month tree. |
| Reduced | opacity only | `data.transition` reduced | Mode changes settle running motion. |
| None | Immediate grid update | zero duration | No animation is started. |
| Selection / enter / exit | Static selection and range styles | none | No decoration on mount. |

The same grid responds to buttons, native dropdowns, keyboard navigation and external controlled
month updates. Week-count height changes immediately. Caller transform/opacity styles take
precedence over the corresponding animation property. No outgoing duplicate steals focus.

## Accessibility

DayPicker owns grid labels, selected/disabled semantics and roving focus. Native month/year
selects stay keyboard reachable. Pass a meaningful `aria-label` when several calendars appear.
DayPicker 9.13.2 keeps its default navigation labels in English even with a date-fns locale;
provide `labels` to localize those strings. Use the `footer` live region or a separate status for selected values. Do not replace a day
with a non-interactive element in a selectable calendar.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Previous/next day or week; crosses month boundaries. |
| Home / End | Start/end of week. |
| Page Up / Page Down | Previous/next month. |
| Shift + Page Up / Page Down | Previous/next year. |
| Enter / Space | Select focused day using the active selection mode. |
| Tab | Move between navigation, caption controls and the roving day target. |

## Validation and data ownership

Calendar renders the caller's selection and disabled matchers. The caller owns business rules,
validation, timezone, serialization and form state. No hidden field or schema is created.
DayPicker's required/min/max/excludeDisabled selection behavior is forwarded unchanged.
In 9.13.2, selecting another date at the multiple-mode max resets selection to that date.
With excludeDisabled, a range crossing a disabled date resets its start to the clicked date.

## Responsive behavior

Cells default to 32px and can be enlarged with `className="[--cell-size:--spacing(10)]"`.
Multiple months stack vertically below md and become a row at md. Provide enough space when
customizing cells, week numbers or month counts. The preview is checked at 390px and 1280px.

## Performance

No layout measurements, duplicate month DOM or animation timers. Only the changing month grid
animates; dates and keyboard focus remain managed by DayPicker. The dependency is pinned to
9.13.2 with date-fns 4.1.0. Pass an explicit defaultMonth/today/timeZone when server and client
must agree across timezone or date boundaries. For SSR dropdown captions, pass an explicit locale
(e.g. enUS from date-fns/locale): the pinned upstream formatter uses the environment locale
when locale is omitted, which can differ between server and browser.

## Notes for AI

Keep the discriminated DayPicker selection props together. Do not introduce validation or
remount with a month key to animate. Prefer Calendar inside Popover for a field, and preserve
custom labels, locale and disabled matchers when composing it.

# Navigation Menu

Site navigation with shared popup content and interruptible sizing.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/navigation-menu
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuTrigger,
  NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuLink } from "@/components/cadence/navigation-menu";

export function SiteNavigation() {
  return (
    <NavigationMenu aria-label="Main navigation">
      <NavigationMenuList>
        <NavigationMenuItem value="learn">
          <NavigationMenuTrigger>Learn</NavigationMenuTrigger>
          <NavigationMenuContent className="w-64">
            <NavigationMenuLink href="/docs">Documentation</NavigationMenuLink>
          </NavigationMenuContent>
        </NavigationMenuItem>
      </NavigationMenuList>
    </NavigationMenu>
  );
}
```

## Controlled navigation

Use a stable item value. `null` closes the popup. Base UI passes change details with the reason
and cancellation methods through unchanged.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = React.useState<string | null>(null);
<NavigationMenu value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>…</NavigationMenu>
```

## Active links and custom rendering

Use `active` for the current route. `render` accepts an element or state callback; custom routing
components must forward native link props and refs.

```tsx
<NavigationMenuLink active render={<a href="/docs" />}>Docs</NavigationMenuLink>
<NavigationMenuTrigger className={state => state.open ? "bg-accent" : ""}>
  Resources
</NavigationMenuTrigger>
```

## Retained content

`keepMounted` keeps inactive content hidden, preserving state across item switches while the popup stays mounted. The default portal unmounts on a complete close, so keepMounted does not retain local state across closing the whole menu. Base UI moves content to the shared
viewport and makes outgoing content inert during its exit. Updating children resizes the same popup.

```tsx
<NavigationMenuContent keepMounted className="w-72">
  <NavigationMenuLink href="/guides">Guides</NavigationMenuLink>
</NavigationMenuContent>
```

## When to use

- Primary site navigation with grouped destinations.
- Desktop resource menus with differently sized panels.
- Navigation that needs pointer, touch and keyboard access to the same links.

## When not to use

- Application commands: use `menubar` or `dropdown-menu`.
- Persistent mobile navigation: use `sidebar` or a `sheet` composition.
- Switching local page content: use `tabs`.

## API

| Part | Props | Defaults and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NavigationMenu` | Base UI Root props, `align` | `align="start"`; `value`/`defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete`, `actionsRef`, `delay`, `closeDelay`, `orientation`, `render`, ref and native nav props pass through. Automatically appends one positioner. |
| `NavigationMenuList` | Base UI List props | List semantics and keyboard navigation. |
| `NavigationMenuItem` | Base UI Item props | Stable `value` associates trigger and content. |
| `NavigationMenuTrigger` | Base UI Trigger props | Native button, supports disabled, render, refs, callback classes/styles. |
| `NavigationMenuContent` | Base UI Content props | Portaled content, `keepMounted=false`; caller classes/styles merge with primitive state. |
| `NavigationMenuLink` | Base UI Link props | Native anchor; `active`, `closeOnClick`, render, refs supported. |
| `NavigationMenuIndicator` | Base UI Icon props | Static arrow within a trigger; no extra animation. |
| `NavigationMenuPositioner` | Base UI Positioner props | `side="bottom"`, `sideOffset=8`, `align="start"`, `alignOffset=0`; anchor, collision, render, refs and state callbacks pass through. |
| `navigationMenuTriggerStyle` | CVA function | Trigger classes for standalone navigation links. |

The pinned Base UI API exports Positioner, rather than Radix's Viewport export or `viewport` root prop.
Positioner contains the popup and viewport. Root already appends it; do not add a second one. Popup and
viewport have additive `data-slot` hooks. Positioner props still follow upstream composition.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Recipe / tokens | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Popup opacity and anchor scale; content opacity | `popup.anchored`, fast clock, scale.in | Native CSS reversal |
| Close / outgoing content | Opacity to zero; popup returns to anchor scale | `exit.fade`, fast clock | Base UI retains exit nodes until completion |
| Switch / update | Shared popup width/height, clamped to available space | `geometry.resize`, slow clock / ease.out | Base UI measures current size before retargeting |
| Reduced | Opacity only; no scale or geometry transition | Fast clock at 0.6×; geometry instant | Live downgrade keeps nodes and focus |
| None | All durations zero, geometry instant | Zeroed CSS tokens | Running transitions finish immediately |

Content switches cross-fade; they do not slide. The positioner follows the active trigger instantly.
Sizing uses Base UI's measured popup variables, not render-time reads or a second animation engine. Trigger activation and in-panel content mutation retarget the resize clock; a value-only controlled switch can adopt the new natural geometry immediately.
Popup and content own token-derived CSS clocks so explicit nested modes and the preview speed work across portals. Caller custom motion must obey the same mode contract.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Enter and leave the navigation without a modal focus trap. |
| ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Move between top-level items in horizontal orientation. |
| ArrowDown / Enter / Space | Open a trigger; Tab enters its content. |
| Escape | Close and return focus to the active trigger. |
| Enter on a link | Follow the native link destination. |

## Accessibility

Root is a navigation landmark; give multiple navigation regions distinct accessible labels. Triggers
expose expanded state and content association. Base UI owns pointer hover, click/touch activation,
focus guards, disabled triggers and outside/Escape dismissal. Closing does not duplicate content or
remount it to reset motion. Cadence removes aria-hidden from Base UI 1.6’s tabbable focus sentinels within this menu; they remain empty generic spans with their original Tab redirection handlers. Keep link text meaningful and keyboard focus rings visible.

## Responsive behavior

Popup width and height are limited by Base UI's available viewport dimensions. Its viewport scrolls
when content exceeds that space. Supply responsive widths/grids for your destinations; the component
does not replace your information architecture with a mobile drawer. Resize updates anchor geometry
immediately in all modes. Reduced and none never tween width/height.

## Performance

T3: one shared popup, native CSS transitions, and Base UI's existing post-commit measurements and
mutation/resize tracking. No additional geometry observer, timer, layout animation loop or persistent
will-change. Two scoped child-list observers repair newly inserted focus sentinels; they disconnect on unmount. Geometry transitions are limited to the popup; nothing transitions top/left. Inactive
content unmounts by default; keepMounted deliberately retains caller state and its DOM cost.

## Notes for AI

Match the Base UI surface, including render, refs and state callback classes/styles. Do not add Radix
asChild or substitute a command menu. Keep stable item values; do not key the viewport on selection.
Use real links, label the landmark, and keep mobile content within available space.

# Resizable

Adjustable split panels with pointer and keyboard resizing.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/resizable
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup } from "@/components/cadence/resizable";

export function Workspace() {
  return (
    <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="horizontal" className="min-h-64 rounded-md border">
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="40%" minSize="20%"><div className="p-4">Explorer</div></ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize explorer" />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize="60%" minSize="40%"><div className="p-4">Editor</div></ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  );
}
```

## Vertical layout

Set `orientation="vertical"` on the group and give it a definite height. The separator's
ARIA orientation describes the divider: horizontal for a vertical group.

```tsx
<ResizablePanelGroup orientation="vertical" style={{ height: 320 }}>
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize="50%">Preview</ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle withHandle aria-label="Resize preview" />
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize="50%">Output</ResizablePanel>
</ResizablePanelGroup>
```

## Collapse and external updates

Use the library's public refs. `defaultLayout` is an initial/persisted layout, not a controlled
value prop. Apply external changes with `groupRef.setLayout`; no controlled API is invented.
`onLayoutChange` reports live updates, while `onLayoutChanged` reports completed changes
and `meta.isUserInteraction`. `onResize` reports pixel and percentage sizes with the prior size.

```tsx
import { useGroupRef, usePanelRef } from "react-resizable-panels";

export function CollapsibleWorkspace() {
  const group = useGroupRef();
  const panel = usePanelRef();
  return (
    <div>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => panel.current?.collapse()}>Collapse</button>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => panel.current?.expand()}>Expand</button>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => panel.current?.resize("55%")}>Resize</button>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => group.current?.setLayout({ files: 40, editor: 60 })}>Reset</button>
      <ResizablePanelGroup groupRef={group} style={{ height: 288 }}>
        <ResizablePanel id="files" panelRef={panel} collapsible minSize="20%" maxSize="60%" defaultSize="40%">Files</ResizablePanel>
        <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize files" />
        <ResizablePanel id="editor" minSize="40%" defaultSize="60%">Editor</ResizablePanel>
      </ResizablePanelGroup>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Editor panes whose widths users adjust.
- Preview/output workspaces with vertical splits.
- Collapsible tool panels with persistent application-owned layouts.

## When not to use

- Static columns: use CSS grid.
- Hidden disclosure content: use Collapsible or Accordion.
- Mobile navigation: use Sheet or Sidebar.

## API

| Export | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `ResizablePanelGroup` | `react-resizable-panels` `GroupProps`; orientation horizontal, resizing enabled, immediate panel preview. |
| `ResizablePanel` | `PanelProps`; min 0%, max 100%, collapsible false, collapsed size 0%, relative resize behavior. |
| `ResizableHandle` | `SeparatorProps` plus optional `withHandle` (unset by default). |

All native attributes/events, string classes, style objects, `elementRef`, `groupRef`,
`panelRef`, constraints, callbacks, disabled state and preview props pass through. This primitive
has no Base UI `render`, `asChild`, or callback class/style API. Group and handle classes merge
caller last. Panel classes and caller styles target the library's inner content element; `elementRef` addresses
its root. Managed flex/display geometry retains library precedence; other caller styles pass through.
Handle children follow upstream: the wrapper renders its optional grip instead of caller children.

Numeric sizes are **pixels**; use strings such as `"40%"` for percentages. Group layouts map
stable panel ids to numeric percentages. Slots: `resizable-panel-group`, `resizable-panel`,
`resizable-handle`. Use `elementRef` for DOM access rather than a generic React ref.

## Motion contract

T0: declared, implemented and documented recipe sets are empty. Direct manipulation is functional
layout, not an authored animation. Pointer, keyboard, collapse/expand and imperative updates apply
immediately in full, reduced and none. No spring, timer, geometry tween, opacity reveal, provider,
`data-motion` or motion hook is shipped. Mode changes preserve the same panel nodes and input state.

| Mode | Authored motion |
| --- | --- |
| full | none; immediate layout |
| reduced | none; immediate layout |
| none | none; immediate layout |

Caller-added animation is application-owned. Do not transition flex or width/height on these panels:
it makes the divider lag behind input and bypasses the geometry recipe budget.

## Accessibility

The primitive supplies focusable separators, `aria-controls`, orientation and value bounds/current
value. Label each handle. Tab focuses the separator; axis arrows resize by 5 percentage points,
Home/End reach permitted limits, Enter toggles the preceding collapsible panel, and F6/Shift+F6
cycle enabled separators. Double-click restores the preceding panel's default size unless disabled.
A locked group disables resizing; disabling only a separator still permits indirect panel resizing.
Keep critical controls outside a collapsible panel so they remain reachable when it is zero-sized.

## Responsive behavior

Constrain the group's height for vertical layouts. Use `min-w-0` on grid parents, percentage constraints
for narrow screens and scrollable inner content for long lines. Orientation changes are caller-owned;
there is no automatic mobile breakpoint. The preview supports both axes at desktop and 390px.
The library adjusts constraints on container resize; at least one panel must preserve relative size.

## Performance

No Cadence animation or extra measurement engine is added. The library owns resize observation and
pointer/keyboard handling. Keep expensive persistence work in `onLayoutChanged`, not every live update.
Percentage defaults can shift slightly during SSR hydration; provide stable ids and consistent initial
layout. This T0 source budget excludes the declared third-party dependency; it is not a total bundle claim.

## Notes for AI

- Use v4 Group/Panel/Separator props and public refs; v3 direction/PanelGroup APIs do not apply.
- Preserve constraints and immediate resizing in all modes.
- Use stable ids when persisting layouts and explicit units for panel sizes.

# Sidebar

Workspace navigation for dashboards and application shells.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/sidebar
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Sidebar, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, SidebarContent, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton } from "@/components/cadence/sidebar";

export function Workspace() {
  return <SidebarProvider>
    <Sidebar><SidebarContent><nav aria-label="Workspace"><SidebarMenu>
      <SidebarMenuItem><SidebarMenuButton render={<a href="/projects" />}>Projects</SidebarMenuButton></SidebarMenuItem>
    </SidebarMenu></nav></SidebarContent></Sidebar>
    <main><SidebarTrigger />Your content</main>
  </SidebarProvider>;
}
```

## Icon navigation

Use `collapsible="icon"` with an icon and text inside each `SidebarMenuButton`. A `tooltip` string
labels the collapsed icon. Keep an accessible name on rendered links. Widths update immediately;
menu children stay mounted on desktop.

## Controlled navigation

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(true);
return <SidebarProvider open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Sidebar collapsible="offcanvas">Navigation</Sidebar>
  <SidebarTrigger />
</SidebarProvider>;
```

The desktop setter writes `sidebar_state=true|false`, path `/`, max-age seven days. It does not read
that cookie. Read it on the server and pass `defaultOpen` when persistence is needed. Supplying
`onOpenChange` delegates state changes to that callback, as upstream does. Mobile state is separate;
`useSidebar()` exposes `openMobile`, `setOpenMobile`, `isMobile`, and `toggleSidebar`.

## When to use

- Persistent workspace navigation in dashboards.
- Application shells with a compact icon rail.
- Navigation that becomes a modal panel on narrow screens.

## When not to use

Use Navigation Menu for short top-level menus and Sheet for a task panel. This component does not
provide routing, permissions, or application state.

## API

### `SidebarProvider`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| defaultOpen | boolean | true | Initial desktop state. |
| open / onOpenChange | boolean / callback | — | Controlled desktop state. |
| style | CSSProperties | — | Overrides `--sidebar-width` (16rem) and `--sidebar-width-icon` (3rem). |
| native div props / ref | native | — | Forwarded to wrapper. |

### `Sidebar`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| side | left / right | left | Physical panel edge. |
| variant | sidebar / floating / inset | sidebar | Surface treatment. |
| collapsible | offcanvas / icon / none | offcanvas | Hide, compact, or remain visible. |
| dir | string | — | Native panel direction in desktop, static and mobile layouts. |
| className / style / ref | native | — | Desktop container; static sidebar or mobile popup respectively. |

`SidebarTrigger` accepts Button props and calls caller `onClick` before toggling. `SidebarRail`
accepts native button props and is excluded from Tab order; the trigger is the keyboard control.
`SidebarInset` renders a main landmark; use it as the application's main, not inside another main.
`SidebarInput` and `SidebarSeparator` accept their corresponding component props.

`SidebarHeader`, `SidebarFooter`, `SidebarContent`, `SidebarGroup`, `SidebarGroupContent`,
`SidebarMenuBadge`, and `SidebarMenuSkeleton` accept div props. Skeleton supports `showIcon=false`;
its deterministic text width avoids hydration mismatch. `SidebarMenu`/`SidebarMenuSub` render ul;
`SidebarMenuItem`/`SidebarMenuSubItem` render li.

`SidebarGroupLabel`, `SidebarGroupAction`, `SidebarMenuAction`, `SidebarMenuButton`, and
`SidebarMenuSubButton` accept Base UI `render` (element or state callback), native props and refs.
MenuButton supports `isActive=false`, `variant="default"|"outline"`, `size="default"|"sm"|"lg"`,
and `tooltip` (string or TooltipContent props). MenuAction supports `showOnHover=false`.
SubButton supports `size="md"|"sm"` and `isActive=false`. Classes merge caller last; native events
and useRender event merging remain available. `useSidebar` requires a provider.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop offcanvas toggle | transform, own-width translation | `layout.move` | Yes, current position and velocity retarget. |

Full springs between the edge and off-edge position; no mounting reveal. Reduced and none update
position immediately, with no animated transform. Gap, icon widths, label margins and visibility
update immediately in every mode. No layout or height tween is authored. Caller `style.transform`
owns that property and suppresses desktop motion. System reduced motion overrides full; live mode
downgrades stop the running spring without replacing the panel.

Mobile delegates `popup.anchored` / `exit.fade` to Sheet. Button press, tooltip popup and Skeleton pulse
are owned by those dependencies, not extra Sidebar recipes. Their effective mode follows the provider.

## Accessibility

Wrap navigation links in a named nav landmark. `isActive` styles the item; add `aria-current="page"`
to the active link yourself. Offcanvas desktop contents are inert while closed. The mobile Sheet
has a hidden title and description, traps focus, dismisses with Escape/outside click and restores
focus. Place a visible close control inside long mobile navigation when needed.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl+B / Cmd+B | Toggle desktop state or mobile sheet. Also applies inside inputs, matching upstream. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Normal links and controls; no menu-style arrow navigation. |
| Enter / Space | Activate the trigger. |
| Escape | Dismiss the mobile sheet. |

## Responsive behavior

Below 768px, collapsible navigation uses an 18rem Sheet. `collapsible="none"` remains static on all
widths. Left/right and all three variants remain supported. Desktop toggles retain child state;
switching between desktop and mobile uses upstream's separate trees and can remount children.
Default mobile closing unmounts content. Store drafts outside Sidebar if they must survive that.

## Performance

Only the desktop offcanvas transform animates. There is no measurement loop, persistent will-change,
timer, width interpolation or validation dependency. Child input values survive desktop state and
motion-mode updates. Render only the navigation items the application needs.

## Notes for AI

Keep the provider, navigation landmark and main content together. Use `render`, never `asChild`.
Do not assume the cookie is read or desktop `open` controls the mobile sheet. Do not animate icon
widths or disclosure height without a separately reviewed measured geometry contract.

# Data Table

An editable payments table with sorting, filtering, selection, visibility, and pagination.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/data-table
```

The block installs TanStack Table **9.3.1** and the Cadence Table, Input, Button,
Checkbox and Dropdown Menu items. Manual installation: copy
`registry/cadence/data-table/index.tsx` to `components/cadence/data-table/index.tsx`,
install those registry dependencies, then install `@tanstack/react-table@9.3.1`.
Keep the relative imports and sibling install tree.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DataTableDemo } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

export function Payments() {
  return <DataTableDemo />;
}
```

This is an editable payments **composition**, not a universal table primitive.
It starts from the [pinned Base example](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/examples/base/data-table-demo.tsx)
and [guide](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/content/docs/components/base/data-table.mdx).
`Payment`, `columns`, and `DataTableDemo` retain that example's exports.
Edit the column definitions and feature registration for your application.
The current [TanStack React documentation](https://tanstack.com/table/latest/docs/framework/react/overview)
describes v9; v8's `useReactTable` and `get*RowModel` options do not apply.

## Application data

```tsx
import { DataTableDemo, type Payment } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

const payments: Payment[] = [
  { id: "invoice-1", email: "lee@example.com", amount: 42, status: "pending" },
];

export function PaymentHistory() {
  return <DataTableDemo data={payments} className="max-w-4xl" />;
}
```

IDs must be unique and stable. Sorting and filtering retain selected IDs; replacing
records does not select a different record at the same array index. The caller
owns removal of stale selections when records disappear. Amounts are USD numbers;
status is `pending | processing | success | failed`. The default is five example
payments. Copy payment ID writes the original ID to the browser clipboard; Email
customer is a real `mailto:` link. Clipboard permission/errors belong to the host.

## Controlled sorting and pagination

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { PaginationState, SortingState } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { DataTableDemo } from "@/components/cadence/data-table";

export function ControlledPayments() {
  const [sorting, setSorting] = useState<SortingState>([]);
  const [pagination, setPagination] = useState<PaginationState>({ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 10 });
  return <DataTableDemo sorting={sorting} onSortingChange={setSorting}
    pagination={pagination} onPaginationChange={setPagination} />;
}
```

Pair each controlled state prop with its matching change callback. Callbacks receive
TanStack value-or-updater functions, so React setters work directly. A state prop
without a callback is read-only; a callback without a state prop observes updates
but takes over updating that slice. Leave both absent for internal state.
The default page size is 10. The header checkbox selects the **current page**;
the status counts selected rows in the filtered collection. Email sorts ascending
then descending, case-insensitively; its filter is a case-insensitive substring.
Filtering resets pagination through TanStack's default auto reset behavior.

## Column visibility and empty results

```tsx
<DataTableDemo columnVisibility={{ status: false }} />
<DataTableDemo columnFilters={[{ id: "email", value: "no-match" }]} />
```

Columns hides Status, Email or Amount. Selection and Actions cannot be hidden.
