A hidden Email column keeps its filter state. Empty results span the number of
**visible** columns. Use a corresponding callback to make either example editable.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller fetches records, decides validity and owns persistence. This block
contains no validation, submission, request orchestration or schema API.
All processing is client-side; server pagination, virtualization, editing,
resizing and multi-column filter controls require adapting the copied composition.

## When to use

- Payment lists with sortable emails and small client-side collections.
- A starting point for an application-specific TanStack v9 composition.
- A native table with page-level selection and column visibility controls.

## When not to use

- Static records: use [Table](/components/table).
- Very large datasets: build caller-owned server pagination or virtualization.
- Spreadsheet navigation or cell editing: this example has native table semantics.

## API

`DataTableDemo` accepts native `div` props (including React 19 ref, events, style,
and classes merged last) on `data-slot="data-table"`. Table parts retain their
existing slots. The native table is named Payments and has a visible focus ring.

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Payment[]` | five sample payments |
| `sorting` | `SortingState` | internal `[]` |
| `columnFilters` | `ColumnFiltersState` | internal `[]` |
| `columnVisibility` | `ColumnVisibilityState` | internal `{}` |
| `rowSelection` | `RowSelectionState` | internal `{}` |
| `pagination` | `PaginationState` | internal `{ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 10 }` |
| `onSortingChange` | `OnChangeFn<SortingState>` | internal setter |
| `onColumnFiltersChange` | `OnChangeFn<ColumnFiltersState>` | internal setter |
| `onColumnVisibilityChange` | `OnChangeFn<ColumnVisibilityState>` | internal setter |
| `onRowSelectionChange` | `OnChangeFn<RowSelectionState>` | internal setter |
| `onPaginationChange` | `OnChangeFn<PaginationState>` | internal setter |

The exported `columns` are the payment-specific TanStack v9 definitions, not an
additional generic public table API. Customize this file rather than passing
arbitrary columns to `DataTableDemo`.

## Motion contract

No row entrance, reorder, resize or layout motion. Sorting, filtering, pagination
and visibility update native markup immediately without keying the table or input
by state. Surviving rows use stable IDs; off-page rows unmount normally.
T2 describes the composed controls; there is no separate table animation runtime.

| Recipe / cause | full | reduced | none |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feedback.press` / Button press | token spring scale | no scale | immediate |
| `state.morph` / checkbox or menu check | opacity and scale | opacity only | zero duration |
| `popup.anchored` / Columns or Actions opens | opacity and scale | opacity only | visible on first frame |
| `exit.fade` / menu closes | opacity and scale exit | opacity only | immediate |

Recipes and timing tokens belong to the installed controls. Dropdown Menu uses
its local `duration.fast` clock, including timeScale and reducedDurationScale,
even through a portal inside a differently configured provider. Live downgrade
drops transforms and `none` removes all motion transitions. No measured geometry,
loop, timer, stagger, or permanent `will-change` is introduced by this block.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Native table headers use `scope="col"`; the sorted header exposes `aria-sort`.
Tab reaches the named filter, column trigger, checkboxes, row actions and page
buttons. Space toggles a focused checkbox; Enter activates buttons. Arrow keys
navigate open menus, Escape dismisses and returns focus. No grid arrow-key model
is added to static cells. Each row checkbox includes its email in the accessible
name; the header is Select all. The filtered selection count is a live status.

## Responsiveness and performance

The toolbar and footer wrap. The native Table wrapper scrolls horizontally at
narrow widths; no data columns disappear automatically. Focus the named table
and use arrow keys to scroll, or use touch/pointer scrolling. The composition is
SSR-compatible with deterministic example data. Keep caller arrays stable where
possible; TanStack recomputes client row models when data/state change. This
block is intended for paginated collections, not an unbounded dataset benchmark.

## Notes for AI

- Keep Base UI `render`, Dropdown Menu groups, native table markup and stable row IDs.
- Register v9 features, row models, sorting and filtering functions explicitly.
- Keep data fetching, validation, stale selection cleanup and URL state caller-owned.
- Preserve all three modes of the composed controls; do not animate table geometry.
- Related: [Table](/components/table), [Checkbox](/components/checkbox),
  [Dropdown Menu](/components/dropdown-menu), [Pagination](/components/pagination).

# Date Picker

Choose a single date or date range from an anchored calendar.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/date-picker
```

The block installs Button, Calendar, Popover, their shared libraries and date-fns
4.1.0. For manual installation copy `registry/cadence/date-picker/index.tsx` to
`components/cadence/date-picker/index.tsx`, install those registry items and
`date-fns@4.1.0` plus `lucide-react`. Keep the sibling tree and relative imports.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";

export function Appointment() {
  return <DatePickerDemo label="Appointment date" />;
}
```

An editable composition, using the [pinned Base example](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/examples/base/date-picker-demo.tsx)
and [guide](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/96da9cc7f1aa10580a3741664e2a77c721206c00/apps/v4/content/docs/components/base/date-picker.mdx),
with new-york-v4's calendar-icon treatment. There is no new date primitive.
The named `DatePickerDemo` export and initially empty single selection remain.
Selection leaves the popup open, including deselection of the selected day.

## Controlled date and clearing

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function ControlledDate() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>();
  return <>
    <DatePickerDemo value={date} onValueChange={setDate} />
    <Button onClick={() => setDate(undefined)}>Clear</Button>
  </>;
}
```

A present `value` prop, including `undefined`, is controlled. Without it,
`defaultValue` initializes internal state and `onValueChange` observes changes.
A controlled value without a callback is read-only. Keep the ownership model
stable. `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` follow Base UI Popover semantics.
The default month is the selected month when the popup mounts; while open,
external selection changes preserve the displayed month and focus tree. To
navigate externally, pair `calendarProps.month` and `onMonthChange` explicitly.

## Range and presets

```tsx
"use client";
import { useState } from "react";
import type { DateRange } from "react-day-picker";
import { DatePickerDemo } from "@/components/cadence/date-picker";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Trip() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange>();
  return <>
    <DatePickerDemo mode="range" label="Travel dates" value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />
    <Button onClick={() => setRange({ from: new Date(2026, 10, 10), to: new Date(2026, 10, 15) })}>Apply preset</Button>
  </>;
}
```

Range mode uses two months by default, matching the guide's range example.
The first click can produce an incomplete range (`from` without `to`); both
endpoints display once complete. DayPicker owns range rules. Pass `min`, `max`,
`excludeDisabled` or `disabled` through `calendarProps` when your application
needs them. Clear with a controlled `undefined` value. Presets are caller actions.

## Disabled dates and birth dates

```tsx
<DatePickerDemo disabled label="Unavailable" />
<DatePickerDemo label="Birth date" calendarProps={{
  captionLayout: "dropdown",
  startMonth: new Date(1920, 0), endMonth: new Date(2026, 11),
  disabled: { after: new Date(2026, 10, 1) },
}} />
```

`disabled` disables the trigger. `calendarProps.disabled` uses DayPicker matchers
for individual days. Dropdown captions and controlled months retain Calendar's
API. Application rules decide acceptable dates; disabling UI is not validation.

## Locale, date input and time

```tsx
import { fr } from "date-fns/locale";

<DatePickerDemo calendarProps={{ locale: fr, weekStartsOn: 1 }} />
```

The trigger uses date-fns `PPP` with the calendar locale (English by default).
Pass Date objects, not ambiguous date strings. Use `new Date(year, monthIndex,
day)` for local calendar dates; `new Date("2026-11-12")` parses as UTC and can
show the previous local day. This block does not serialize or convert time zones.
For DayPicker `timeZone`, supply dates constructed for that zone, such as
DayPicker's `TZDate`, so trigger and calendar share civil-date fields. The caller
owns persistence, DST policy and UTC conversion.

The upstream guide also illustrates input, time and natural-language compositions.
This copied block focuses on single/range calendar selection. Compose a labelled
native date/time Input alongside it if needed; keep parsing and text drafts in
the host application. No natural-language parser dependency or text validation
is installed. Locale alone does not set direction; set `dir="rtl"` on the host
and `calendarProps.dir="rtl"` when required.

## Validation and data ownership

The caller owns validation, parsing, submission, storage, fetching and time-zone
policy. Use `triggerProps` for `aria-invalid` or `aria-describedby`. No schema,
resolver, validation callback or hidden form input is added. Serialize selected
values explicitly in the application.

## When to use

- Appointment dates and optional calendar selection.
- Travel ranges, with application-owned presets and constraints.
- A starting composition to edit for your application's form.

## When not to use

- An always-visible date grid: use [Calendar](/components/calendar).
- Time-only entry: use a labelled [Input](/components/input) with `type="time"`.
- Free-form language parsing: supply your application's parser and draft state.

## API

`DatePickerDemoProps` is a discriminated union; range values require `mode="range"`.
Native div props, React 19 ref/cleanup, classes and styles go to `data-slot="date-picker"`.

| Prop | Type | Default / behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `"single" \| "range"` | `"single"` |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | `Date` or `DateRange` | initially empty; present value is controlled |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Date \| undefined) => void`, range equivalent | observes selection/deselection |
| `label` | `string` | `"Choose date"`; accessible trigger prefix and popup title |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `"Pick a date"` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false`, disables trigger |
| `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` | Popover props | Base UI ownership and event details |
| `calendarProps` | corresponding optional-selection Calendar props | autoFocus, selected default month; range two months |
| `triggerProps` | `ButtonProps` | outline button; caller classes/styles/callbacks last |
| `contentProps` | `PopoverContent` props | start-aligned, available-size constrained, scrollable |

Selection props (`mode`, `selected`, `onSelect`, `required`) are owned by the
composition. Use Calendar directly for required/multiple selection. Other
calendar overrides remain caller-owned, including month, locale, focus and
components. A custom render must retain a focusable button and the supplied props.

## Motion contract

T2 describes existing control motion. No date label animation, layout tween,
selection-keyed remount, new recipe or runtime is added.

| Recipe / cause | full | reduced | none |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feedback.press` / trigger press | token spring scale | no scale | immediate |
| `popup.anchored` / open | opacity and token scale | opacity only | visible first frame |
| `exit.fade` / close | opacity and scale | opacity only | immediate |
| `data.transition` / calendar month | token horizontal translation and opacity | opacity only | immediate |

Popover resolves its own `duration.fast` clock with timeScale and reducedDurationScale
inside the portal. Nested full can recover under outer none; OS reduce still wins.
Live reduced drops scale and live none cancels transitions immediately. Calendar
cancels its WAAPI effect on mode changes without replacing the grid or focused day.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Tab reaches the named trigger; Space/Enter opens the dialog. Calendar focuses the
selected enabled day or its initial focus target. Arrow keys move days, Home/End
move within the week, PageUp/PageDown navigate months. Escape dismisses and returns
focus to the trigger. Selecting a day keeps the popup open. Screen readers hear
the popup title, grid month, day labels and selected states. Range selection retains
DayPicker's grid model. Button names include the label and formatted selection.

## Responsiveness and performance

The trigger truncates long labels within the available width. The popup is bounded
by Base UI's available width/height and scrolls; range months stack on small screens
and sit side by side on desktop. No document overflow is required. Deterministic
example dates are SSR-compatible; empty uncontrolled selection renders without
reading the clock. DayPicker's current-month fallback depends on the host clock;
pass `defaultMonth` and `today` for deterministic server/client calendars.

## Notes for AI

- Keep this a registry block with namespaced dependencies and relative imports.
- Keep value presence semantics so controlled undefined clears correctly.
- Preserve stable Calendar identities and Base UI focus/render/event semantics.
- Keep locale and civil-date/time-zone policy explicit in the caller.
- Related: [Calendar](/components/calendar), [Popover](/components/popover), [Button](/components/button).

# Attachment

Displays file media, metadata, caller-owned upload state, and actions.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/attachment
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Attachment, AttachmentMedia, AttachmentContent, AttachmentTitle,
  AttachmentDescription, AttachmentActions, AttachmentAction,
} from "@/components/cadence/attachment";

export function FileCard({ onRemove }: { onRemove: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Attachment>
      <AttachmentMedia aria-hidden="true">PDF</AttachmentMedia>
      <AttachmentContent>
        <AttachmentTitle>report.pdf</AttachmentTitle>
        <AttachmentDescription>PDF · 2.4 MB</AttachmentDescription>
      </AttachmentContent>
      <AttachmentActions>
        <AttachmentAction aria-label="Remove report.pdf" onClick={onRemove}>×</AttachmentAction>
      </AttachmentActions>
    </Attachment>
  );
}
```

## Upload state

Pass `state="idle"`, `"uploading"`, `"processing"`, `"error"` or `"done"` from your
application. Uploading and processing pulse the title; the description carries
readable status even with animation disabled. An error needs text explaining the
failure. Set `aria-busy` on the appropriate region and use a separate polite status
for meaningful milestones, rather than announcing every progress update.

```tsx
<Attachment state="uploading" aria-busy="true">
  <AttachmentContent>
    <AttachmentTitle>report.pdf</AttachmentTitle>
    <AttachmentDescription>Uploading · 64%</AttachmentDescription>
  </AttachmentContent>
</Attachment>
```

## Images and sizes

Use `AttachmentMedia variant="image"` with a native image and meaningful alt text.
`orientation="vertical"` stacks it above the metadata; horizontal is the default.
Sizes are `default`, `sm` and `xs`. The media is dimmed while work is in progress.
Supply image URLs yourself; the component never creates or revokes object URLs.

## Trigger and independent actions

`AttachmentTrigger` fills the card behind `AttachmentActions`. Give the empty
trigger an accessible name. It defaults to a non-submitting button; `render`
accepts an element or render function, preserving Base UI event/ref merging.
Actions default to ghost Button with icon-xs size and accept Button's callbacks,
native props and `render`. Keep actions in AttachmentActions so their stacking
order leaves them independently reachable.

```tsx
<AttachmentTrigger render={<a href="/files/report.pdf" download aria-label="Download report.pdf" />} />
```

## Scrollable groups

Wrap cards in `AttachmentGroup` for a snapping horizontal row. Native scrolling
is immediate and never smoothed by this component. For presentational cards give
the group `tabIndex={0}`, `role="group"` and an accessible name; interactive cards
can be reached with Tab. Allow the group to shrink within its parent.

```tsx
<AttachmentGroup tabIndex={0} role="group" aria-label="Selected files">
  <Attachment orientation="vertical" size="sm">
    <AttachmentMedia variant="image"><img src={previewUrl} alt="Selected workspace" /></AttachmentMedia>
    <AttachmentContent><AttachmentTitle>workspace.png</AttachmentTitle></AttachmentContent>
  </Attachment>
</AttachmentGroup>
```

## When to use

File previews in composers, upload lists, or message attachments with caller-owned
metadata and optional open/remove/retry actions.

## When not to use

Use Input for native file selection, Progress for a standalone percentage, and
Item for generic content that does not represent a file. Attachment does not
implement an uploader, drop zone, file parser or streaming message runtime.

## API

| Part | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `Attachment` | Native div props; state `done`, size `default`, orientation `horizontal` |
| `AttachmentMedia` | Native div props; variant `icon` or `image`, default `icon` |
| `AttachmentContent` | Native div props; wraps metadata |
| `AttachmentTitle` | Native span props; filename, busy opacity loop |
| `AttachmentDescription` | Native span props; metadata/status text |
| `AttachmentActions` | Native div props; independent action layer |
| `AttachmentAction` | All Button props; size `icon-xs`, variant falls back to `ghost` |
| `AttachmentTrigger` | Base UI useRender button props; type `button` without render; render element/function |
| `AttachmentGroup` | Native div props; horizontal scroll and snap |

Every part preserves its upstream `attachment-*` data-slot (root: `attachment`).
Native refs, styles and events pass through; classes merge last. Root also exposes
`data-state`, `data-size`, `data-orientation`; media exposes `data-variant`.
No File or request state is stored internally. There is no default upload action.

## Motion contract

| Cause | Recipe | Full | Reduced | None |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Uploading/processing title | `data.transition` | Opacity pulse via theme `animate-pulse` | Same opacity loop, no transform | `animate-none`, opacity 1 |
| Default action pressed | `feedback.press` | Button token spring/press scale | No scale | Instant, no scale |

Continuous timing comes from the project's `--animate-pulse` theme token. This
replaces upstream's travelling shimmer with opacity to stay in the motion budget.
Root/title and default actions expose `data-motion`; live none cancels the loop
without replacing nodes. State, removal, size, orientation and media updates are
immediate. No entry, exit, layout or geometry recipe is implied. Custom render
controls can own their own feedback as with Button.

## Keyboard interactions

Tab reaches triggers and actions separately. Enter/Space activate default buttons;
a rendered link uses native link behaviour. Disabled actions retain Button's native
semantics. A focusable group scrolls with arrow keys; Tab also reveals off-screen
interactive cards. Removal focus policy belongs to the caller.

## Accessibility

Name every icon-only action and overlay trigger, retain meaningful image alt text,
and describe failures in text. The trigger has a visible focus ring. Avoid nested
interactive elements inside triggers. Provide a polite live region for upload
milestones outside a busy region. Truncated filenames remain in the DOM; a title
attribute or your own details view can expose their full visual text.

## Validation and data ownership

The application owns native file input `name`, `accept`, `multiple`, `required`,
File objects, form submission, validation, upload progress, requests, cancel/retry,
URLs and URL cleanup. Attachment forwards `aria-invalid`/`data-invalid` when given;
`state="error"` only styles a supplied failure. It never decides which file is valid.
The preview's file input reports the selected filename locally and makes no request.

## Responsiveness and performance

Cards cap at their parent's width; long names truncate. Groups scroll horizontally
with no document overflow when their parent can shrink. Large lists should be
paginated or virtualized by the application. The busy opacity loop uses CSS with
no per-frame JavaScript or layout reads; none stops it on the next style update.
No @shadcn/react dependency or streaming runtime is needed for this pinned API.

## AI usage notes

Compose these nine parts; keep upload state and file lifecycle in your application.
Do not infer a network operation from the visual `state` value. Prefer stable file
IDs as keys so a progress update preserves focus and the native input. There is no
message streaming dependency and no reason to remount a composer when a file changes.

## Related components

[Button](/components/button) supplies actions, [Input](/components/input) supplies
native file selection, [Progress](/components/progress) displays known progress,
and [Code Block](/components/code-block) displays textual file contents.

# Bubble

Displays conversational content with variants, grouping, reactions, and polymorphic surfaces.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/bubble
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Bubble, BubbleContent, BubbleGroup, BubbleReactions } from "@/components/cadence/bubble";

export function Conversation() {
  return (
    <BubbleGroup className="gap-8 py-5">
      <Bubble align="end"><BubbleContent>Ready for review?</BubbleContent></Bubble>
      <Bubble variant="muted">
        <BubbleContent>The registry is ready.</BubbleContent>
        <BubbleReactions role="img" aria-label="Reaction: thumbs up">👍</BubbleReactions>
      </Bubble>
    </BubbleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Variants and alignment

Choose default, secondary, muted, tinted, outline, ghost or destructive. Bubbles
cap at 80% of their container; ghost can use its full width. Start is the default
alignment; end aligns a bubble to the opposite inline edge. Include readable error
context for destructive content so color is not the only signal. Destructive uses
a tinted background and destructive border with foreground text to retain readable
contrast in both themes.

```tsx
<Bubble variant="destructive" align="end">
  <BubbleContent>Message failed. Try again from the message actions.</BubbleContent>
</Bubble>
```

## Consecutive messages

BubbleGroup groups surfaces from the same sender. It supplies a small gap; leave
more vertical space when reactions overlap. Set alignment on each Bubble. Names,
avatars, timestamps and conversation semantics belong to your surrounding UI.

```tsx
<BubbleGroup className="gap-8">
  <Bubble variant="muted"><BubbleContent>First thought.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
  <Bubble variant="muted"><BubbleContent>One more detail.</BubbleContent></Bubble>
</BubbleGroup>
```

## Links and buttons

BubbleContent accepts a Base UI render element or function. Use a real button with
an explicit type or an anchor with href; their text provides the accessible name.
Native handlers and refs, including React 19 ref cleanup, are merged by Base UI.

```tsx
<Bubble variant="outline">
  <BubbleContent render={<a href="/components/attachment" />}>View attachments</BubbleContent>
</Bubble>
```

## Reactions

Side defaults to bottom and align to end. Both accept the opposite edge. The row
uses static positioning transforms, never animated movement. Label emoji-only
rows as a single image; for interactive reactions supply named buttons and their
pressed state instead. Leave vertical space for the overlapping row.

```tsx
<BubbleReactions side="top" align="start" role="img" aria-label="Reactions: thumbs up and fire">
  <span>👍</span><span>🔥</span>
</BubbleReactions>
```

## Updating text

Keep the message ID and rendered element stable when adding text. Children update
immediately without replaying entry, moving focus or animating measured height.
The application owns chunking, message IDs, transport, cancellation, retry and
scroll anchoring. This component neither parses Markdown nor orchestrates a stream.

## When to use

Use for conversational text, quoted replies, suggestion buttons and short
structured output; combine surfaces into a caller-owned conversation layout.

## When not to use

Use Attachment for file metadata, Code Block for syntax-highlighted source, and
Alert for a page-level notice. Bubble supplies a surface rather than a complete
chat, message scroller, composer or streaming runtime.

## API

| Part | Props and defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `Bubble` | Native div props; variant default/secondary/muted/tinted/outline/ghost/destructive (default: default), align start/end (default: start) |
| `BubbleGroup` | Native div props; groups consecutive bubbles |
| `BubbleContent` | Base UI useRender div props; render element or function |
| `BubbleReactions` | Native div props; side top/bottom (default: bottom), align start/end (default: end) |

All four parts retain upstream bubble-* slots (root: bubble), native styles,
refs and events. Classes merge last; Bubble styles merge after its local clock.
Bubble exposes data-variant, data-align and data-motion; reactions expose data-side
and data-align. No additional message-state or validation API is introduced.

## Motion contract

| Cause | Recipe | Full | Reduced | None |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New Bubble enters | `data.transition` | Opacity 0→1, duration.base / ease.out | Opacity only, duration ×0.6 | Opacity 1 on first frame, zero duration |

CSS @starting-style performs a one-shot entry. The duration resolves locally through
cm.transition("data.transition"), including provider timeScale, so an inner full
scope restores its clock inside outer none. Reduced drops animated transforms;
this recipe uses opacity in full too. Live none cancels entry on the same node.
Existing text, variants, alignment, reactions and resize update immediately. Removal
is immediate; there is no exit or layout animation. Caller-provided motion is caller-owned.

## Keyboard interactions

Presentational surfaces add no tab stops. Tab reaches rendered buttons, links and
reaction buttons. Enter activates buttons/links; Space activates buttons. Interactive
BubbleContent has a visible focus ring. Appending text preserves the same focused
node. The application owns focus after removing a message.

## Accessibility

Keep conversation-level semantics on a surrounding labelled region. Supply readable
sender/error context and label reactions. Avoid nested interactive content inside
button/link bubbles. Announce meaningful completed updates in a separate polite
status region when needed; announcing every chunk can overwhelm assistive technology.

## Responsiveness and performance

Long words wrap within a shrinking container. Reactions overlap vertically; give
rows sufficient space and keep reaction collections compact. Rich content can use
ghost with its own overflow treatment. Entry changes only opacity; no layout reads,
per-frame JavaScript, timers or forced remounts. Application pagination or virtualization
owns very large histories. No @shadcn/react dependency is needed for this pinned API.

## AI usage notes

Compose the four parts with stable message IDs. Text and reaction state remain in
your application. Use Collapsible for optional show-more UI and Tooltip/Popover for
metadata; those components keep their own motion contracts. Do not invent streaming,
validation or networking props on Bubble.

## Related components

[Attachment](/components/attachment), [Code Block](/components/code-block),
[Collapsible](/components/collapsible), [Tooltip](/components/tooltip),
[Popover](/components/popover).

# Table of Contents

Section navigation for documentation, guides, and long articles.

## Installation

```install
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toc
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Toc } from "@/components/cadence/toc";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-8 md:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_12rem]">
      <article>
        <h2 id="overview" className="scroll-mt-24">
          Overview
        </h2>
        <p>Introduce the topic here.</p>
        <h2 id="details" className="scroll-mt-24">
          Details
        </h2>
        <p>Explain the details here.</p>
      </article>
      <aside>
        <Toc
          className="sticky top-24"
          items={[
            { id: "overview", title: "Overview" },
            { id: "details", title: "Details" },
          ]}
        />
      </aside>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Nested sections

Pass `depth: 3` for a subsection. Entries stay in document order and indent one level. The caller supplies unique heading ids and readable labels; Toc does not parse Markdown. Each card uses its own id prefix so its links cannot target the surrounding documentation.

<ComponentExample name="nested" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId } from "react";
import { Toc } from "@/components/cadence/toc";

export function Nested() {
  const id = useId();
  const items = [
    { id: `${id}-api`, title: "API" },
    { id: `${id}-props`, title: "Props", depth: 3 },
    { id: `${id}-keyboard`, title: "Keyboard" },
  ] as const;
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-6 sm:grid-cols-2">
      <Toc items={items} label="Reference sections" />
      <div className="grid gap-4 text-sm">
        <section>
          <h3 id={items[0].id} className="scroll-mt-24 font-medium">
            API
          </h3>
          <p className="mt-1 text-muted-foreground">Component reference.</p>
          <h4 id={items[1].id} className="mt-3 scroll-mt-24 font-medium">
            Props
          </h4>
          <p className="mt-1 text-muted-foreground">Caller-supplied options.</p>
        </section>
        <section>
          <h3 id={items[2].id} className="scroll-mt-24 font-medium">
            Keyboard
          </h3>
          <p className="mt-1 text-muted-foreground">Use Tab and Enter on native links.</p>
        </section>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled active section

Supply `activeId` when a router or your observer owns the current section; an empty string clears the highlight. This disables automatic window tracking. The external Mark actions update only this instance, while its delegated link handler keeps caller state in sync with link activation.

<ComponentExample name="controlled" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Toc } from "@/components/cadence/toc";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button";

export function Controlled() {
  const id = useId();
  const items = [
    { id: `${id}-overview`, title: "Overview" },
    { id: `${id}-details`, title: "Details" },
  ] as const;
  const [activeId, setActiveId] = useState<string>(items[0].id);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-5">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setActiveId(items[0].id)}>
          Mark Overview
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setActiveId(items[1].id)}>
          Mark Details
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setActiveId("")}>
          Clear highlight
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Toc
        items={items}
        activeId={activeId}
        label="Controlled sections"
        onClick={(event) => {
          const link =
            event.target instanceof Element ? event.target.closest<HTMLAnchorElement>("a[data-toc-id]") : null;
          if (link) setActiveId(link.dataset.tocId ?? "");
        }}
      />
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-6 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {items.map((item) => (
          <h3 key={item.id} id={item.id} className="scroll-mt-24 font-normal">
            {item.title}
          </h3>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Scroll tracking

Without `activeId`, Toc follows headings on window scroll, resize and initial layout. For a bounded article, the caller tracks that scrolling host and supplies `activeId`, as in this example. Scroll the complete article or activate its links: navigation uses the real scroll container and the wrapped label determines the indicator height. The caller keeps entries and heading ids aligned; it does not add another smooth-scroll clock.

<ComponentExample name="scroll-tracking" />

```tsx
"use client";

import { useId, useState } from "react";
import { Toc } from "@/components/cadence/toc";

export function ScrollTracking() {
  const id = useId();
  const items = [
    { id: `${id}-overview`, title: "Overview" },
    { id: `${id}-installation`, title: "Installation" },
    { id: `${id}-usage`, title: "Usage with longer section titles that wrap across lines" },
    { id: `${id}-api`, title: "API" },
  ] as const;
  const [activeId, setActiveId] = useState<string>(items[0].id);
  const paragraphs = [
    "Choose a section link or scroll this article. Its reading indicator follows the section nearest the top of this scrolling region.",
    "Install the component, then supply the same stable heading ids to both the article and the navigation. Each example here owns a separate id prefix.",
    "Long section titles wrap without widening the navigation rail. The indicator follows the full label height. The article keeps its native keyboard and pointer scrolling.",
    "The caller owns the entries, labels and scroll container. Toc supplies the links, current-section semantics and motion-aware navigation to their real targets.",
  ] as const;
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full min-w-0 gap-5 sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_10rem]">
      <section
        aria-label="Example article"
        tabIndex={0}
        className="h-80 min-w-0 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain rounded-md border p-4 text-sm outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-ring"
        onScroll={(event) => {
          const host = event.currentTarget;
          const top =
            host.getBoundingClientRect().top + host.clientTop + Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(host).paddingTop);
          let current: string = items[0].id;
          for (const item of items) {
            const heading = document.getElementById(item.id);
            if (heading && heading.getBoundingClientRect().top <= top + 1) current = item.id;
          }
          if (host.scrollTop + host.clientHeight >= host.scrollHeight - 1) current = items.at(-1)?.id ?? items[0].id;
          setActiveId(current);
        }}
      >
        {items.map((item, index) => (
          <section key={item.id} className="min-h-64 pb-6">
            <h3 id={item.id} className="scroll-mt-4 font-medium">
              {item.title}
            </h3>
            <p className="mt-3 leading-relaxed text-muted-foreground">{paragraphs[index]}</p>
          </section>
        ))}
      </section>
      <Toc items={items} activeId={activeId} label="Article sections" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## When to use

- Component reference pages with installation, usage, and API sections.
- Long guides whose sections need direct links.
- Articles with nested headings and a reading position indicator.

## When not to use

- Page hierarchy: use Breadcrumb.
- Navigation between different pages: use Sidebar or Navigation Menu.
- Switching panels that hide other content: use Tabs.

## API

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly TocEntry[]` | required | Entries in document order; empty arrays render nothing. |
| `label` | `string` | `"On this page"` | Visible title and accessible navigation label. |
| `activeId` | `string` | automatic | Controlled current heading id; disables automatic tracking. |
| `scrollOffset` | `number` | `96` | Pixels below the viewport top for automatic tracking. |
| `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. |
| native nav props | `ComponentProps<"nav">` | – | Includes ref, style, aria attributes, and event handlers. |

`TocEntry` has `id: string`, `title: string`, and optional `depth: 2 | 3` (default `2`).
Slots are `toc`, `toc-title`, `toc-track`, `toc-rail`, `toc-indicator`, `toc-list`, `toc-item`, and `toc-link`.

## Motion contract

One persistent indicator follows the active entry. Its top and bottom edges use the shared physics
spring, then render as translation and vertical scale on a one-pixel base. Wrapped labels determine
the destination's length. Edges stay inside the rail, and interrupted movement preserves velocity.
Text and `aria-current` follow the current section immediately. Activating a link smoothly scrolls
the actual scrolling host to its heading in full mode. The destination respects the heading's scroll
margin and the host's scroll padding; movement stays within the host's scroll bounds.

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active section or label size changes | Indicator translateY / scaleY | `layout.shared` / `spring.morph` | Yes; the existing indicator follows the latest target. |
| Section link activation | Native scroll offset | `scroll.navigate` / `duration.page` / `ease.inOut` | Yes; another link retargets from the current position. |
| Initial measurement / restored selection | Instant placement, no entrance | — | — |
| reduced | Instant indicator placement and section navigation | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. |
| none | Instant placement and navigation, no animation clock | — | Stops springs; completes an active navigation before paint. |

Zero provider timeScale also places the indicator immediately. Restoring full motion keeps the
settled position until the next section or size change. A ResizeObserver supplies geometry; no
layout is read during render. Navigation uses one token-backed tween, with no separate CSS/native
smooth-scroll clock. Wheel, touch, pointer input, scrolling keys, resizing, history traversal and
external hash changes cancel it at the current position. Positive clock changes retime the current
trip; reduced/none or zero clock complete it immediately. No interrupted trip restarts later.
The site's mobile disclosure stays instant. Initial hashes, reload, history traversal and no-JS
links keep native behavior; only an explicit unmodified section link activation starts the recipe.

## Accessibility

- A labelled `nav` contains an ordered list of native links.
- Tab and Shift+Tab move between links; Enter activates the same navigation as a primary click.
- The active link has `aria-current="location"` and a stronger text weight. The decorative indicator is hidden from assistive technology.
- Heading targets need matching, unique ids. Offset their scroll margin to account for sticky headers.
- Native anchors remain usable before hydration and without JavaScript. Automatic tracking requires JavaScript.
- Navigation preserves unrelated URL parameters and history state, pushes the new fragment and notifies hashchange listeners. Back/forward use native scroll restoration.
- Completion focuses the heading without scrolling a second time. A temporary `tabindex="-1"` is removed on blur/unmount; caller-supplied tabindex is preserved. Interrupted navigation never steals focus.
- Modified/new-tab clicks and caller-cancelled clicks retain native behavior.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move between native section links. |
| Enter | Scroll to the focused link's heading, update the fragment and focus the heading on completion. |
| Scrolling keys / Tab / Escape | Interrupt an ongoing smooth navigation. |

The indicator never receives focus or replaces a link when its destination changes.

## Responsiveness and performance

The component fills its parent and wraps long labels. The caller owns placement, sticky position,
height limits, and overflow. For documentation layouts, place it in a sticky right column with an
independently scrollable list. Smaller viewports can use a native disclosure near the title; a
floating disclosure list avoids moving the article when opened.

Automatic tracking uses passive window scroll events,
resize events, and a ResizeObserver, with cleanup on unmount. It reads heading positions in those callbacks,
updates state only when the active id changes, and selects the final heading at the page bottom.
It tracks headings present when mounted; remount after dynamically replacing the document or pass new items.
The server renders the first entry as current; hydration corrects it for a deep link or restored scroll position.
Before measurement, a static border marks the current link, including without JavaScript. The first
measured position is immediate. The indicator remains mounted through selection and mode changes.
The indicator's two edge values animate; the list's layout does not interpolate. Section navigation
measures its destination once on activation, then writes native offsets without per-frame layout reads.
A ResizeObserver tracks
wrapped labels, font changes, and a mobile disclosure becoming visible. Motion and the shared
Cadence provider/runtime are installed dependencies; a provider is optional and system reduced
motion is respected standalone. The T3 source budget is 12 KB gzip; dependency and page budgets
are measured separately.

## Notes for AI

- Build the list from the same heading tree that renders the article so links and ids cannot drift.
- Use this Cadence original for document navigation; it has no pinned shadcn counterpart.
- Do not use a component instance to generate heading ids or to own application routing.
